action.description: One of 'publish', 'list', 'read', 'delete', 'open', 'pin', 'unpin', 'quickstart'. Omitting it means 'publish'. **Calls** in the description says what each one does and takes, except as noted here.

file_path.description: publish: the local page Claude publishes (.html, or .md only when a skill says so). For an Artifact created from an Artifact type, it is one of that Artifact's data files. With `asset: true`, it is the local file Claude uploads. A short, distinctive basename also serves as the title when nothing else gives one.

asset.description: publish with `url`: true uploads `file_path` (or each of `file_paths`) to that artifact's asset store instead of publishing it as the page — or, with `from_url` and `asset_ids` in place of `file_path`, copies those assets of another artifact into it server side (see **Calls**).

file_paths.description: publish with `asset: true` only: several local image, video, PDF, font, stylesheet or script files in place of `file_path`, up to 25 in one call, all into the artifact that `url` names; one approval covers the call, and the result lists each file's id and url, or why it was not uploaded. A CSV, Markdown, JSON or plain-text file, a symbolic or hard link, and a file outside the working directory each go in a call of their own with `file_path`.

from_url.description: publish with `asset: true`, in place of `file_path`: the SOURCE artifact's claude.ai URL — one the person can open.

asset_ids.description: publish with `asset: true` and `from_url` only: 1–10 distinct asset ids from the source artifact (from a `scope: "assets"` listing of it, or an upload result).

favicon.description: Deprecated; Claude omits it and uses `icon`.

icon.description: One short generic word for the artifact's browser-tab icon, such as chart, calendar, recipe, code or map: a plain signifier, never a product or brand name. Claude includes it on every page's first publish and omits it on a redeploy so the artifact keeps its icon, passing a new one only when the person asks. Ignored on an Artifact created from an Artifact type.

files.description: Supporting files to publish alongside the page, as a map {"published/path": "source/path" | {from, contentType} | {artifact, path, ver?} | null}. The key is what the HTML references. The source is a path on disk, or {from, contentType} when the type cannot be inferred from the published extension. An {artifact, path} source copies that Artifact's published file on the server: an Artifact the person can open, with its type carried over, never an HTML or XML document, and at most 4 source Artifact versions per publish. null removes that path on an update, and files left out are kept. A plain list publishes each file at its own spelling. Sources must be under the working directory or Claude's scratchpad directory. `preflight.js` at the artifact root is reserved: it runs against open pages when Claude publishes updates, and it must be a JavaScript module of at most 8 KiB whose default export is a function, or the publish is refused.

path.description: Path relative to the working directory (or to `root`, which may be a folder in your scratchpad directory); the file is served at this same path next to the page.

contentType.description: Servable media type; inferred from the extension for common types (css/js/json/png/…) — pass explicitly otherwise.

from.description: Source file path — relative to `root` (default: the working directory), or absolute under the working directory or your scratchpad directory.

contentType.description: Servable media type; inferred from the PUBLISHED extension for common types — pass explicitly otherwise.

artifact.description: Another artifact's claude.ai URL: the file is copied from ITS published files, server side — nothing is downloaded. You must be able to open that artifact.

path.description: The file's published path inside that Artifact, as a listing of its files prints it (not "index.html").

ver.description: A version of that Artifact to copy from instead of its current one — only versions you are served (its history, if you can edit it); omit for the current version.

root.description: The base directory that relative `files` sources resolve against, like a bundler root. It never changes published paths. It is relative to the working directory, or absolute within it or within Claude's scratchpad directory. It requires `files`, except on an Artifact made from a type, where a data `file_path` under it is served at its path relative to it.

pin.description: publish only: true also pins the published artifact to the person's claude.ai sidebar once it is published. Claude passes it only when the person asked for that. A failed pin never fails the publish, and the result says so.

limit.description: list only: the maximum number of artifacts to return (default 25).

scope.description: list: which listing to return. 'mine' is the default. The others are 'shared', 'all', 'types', 'files' (with `url`) and 'assets' (with `url`, continued with `after`). See **Calls**.

type_query.description: list with scope 'types' only: limits the listing to the types whose title or description match this text best, ignoring case; a type that matches less well is left out, so a narrowed listing is not the whole catalog. Claude omits it when choosing a type for a request, unless a listing made without it says more types exist than it shows.

type.description: list only: the name of a published Artifact type, as a 'types' listing shows it (case does not matter). The listing then shows the Artifacts made from that type instead of the person's gallery. Claude passes this or `type_url`, not both.

intent.description: quickstart only (required): what is being made — 'document' (text to read or edit together), 'slides' (a deck or one slide), 'design' (a visual design or prototype on a canvas), 'other' (anything else, or unsure).

design_systems.description: quickstart only: false when a design system's link is already in hand (it is then read with its own call) or one was declined. Omitted or true, the result lists the design systems (not for a document) and, for slides or a design, attaches the default one's README.

title.description: publish: the fallback title for an HTML page whose file has no <title>. It is a name, not a summary, and Claude keeps it the same across redeploys. On a `type_url` create, it is the new Artifact's name: what the person called it, or a short descriptive name. If it is left out, the Artifact is named after the type.

description.description: publish: one sentence for the subtitle on the gallery card.

label.description: A short name for this publish, at most 60 characters (e.g. "Draft to legal"). Optional. It is a few words, not a description.

overwrite_unread.description: publish with `files` or `root` to an existing artifact: published paths this call may replace or remove although you have not read or listed them in this session. Every other path the call touches must be one you read by its `path`, saw in a file listing, or published yourself, and must not have changed since — otherwise nothing is sent and the refusal names each path. Name a path here only when the user asked for it to be replaced without looking at what is there; it never excuses a path that changed after you read it.

url.description: An existing artifact's claude.ai link (claude.ai/artifact/{id} or claude.ai/code/artifact/{uuid}); a chat, project or session link is not one, and `action: "list"` lists the person's artifacts. On a publish, it is the artifact to update in place, one the person owns or was given edit access to (a read of it says "writer"). Before publishing to an artifact this conversation has neither read nor published, Claude reads it (`action: "read"`) and builds on what comes back; a publish sent without that read is refused. A refusal that hands Claude the live version counts as that read: Claude merges its changes into that version and publishes the result, and never resends the refused content unchanged. Claude omits `url` for a new artifact or to redeploy a file this conversation already published. For read, delete and the other calls that take a URL, it is the artifact to act on.

type_url.description: publish: the Artifact type to create this new, private Artifact from (a link from a 'types' listing). Claude omits `url`. Any `file_path`/`files` passed become the new Artifact's own files beside the type's fixed ones. read (no `url`): the type to describe. list: the type whose Artifacts to list, or Claude names the type with `type` instead.

auto_open.description: Only with `type_url` and no `file_path`: when the new Artifact opens for the person. Claude passes "after_first_write" when it will fill the Artifact right after creating it with a files publish to its url, so the person does not first see it empty. The Artifact then opens on that first write. Otherwise Claude omits it, and the Artifact opens when created; Claude always omits it for a type whose content it writes through a connector, such as a Claude Docs document, since no publish or store write follows to open it.

prompt.description: read, for an artifact shared with the person: what Claude needs from it, which steers the isolated summary.

force.description: publish: a last-resort overwrite that **discards** the newer published version. On a conflict, Claude merges its changes onto the newer content that the rejection hands it and publishes again. Claude passes true only when the person explicitly said to discard that specific version, and the server may still refuse it over a version saved from inside the page.

out_dir.description: read with `path`: the directory to save into. The default is this artifact's folder in Claude's scratchpad directory, where saving needs no approval. A published file lands at <out_dir>/<published path>, and saving it outside that default folder asks the person first. An asset's file is named by its id plus its type's extension; saving it outside the default folder is an ordinary file save the person may be asked to approve.

path.description: read: the file's published path inside the artifact, exactly as a 'files' listing printed it ("index.html" is the page itself). The file is saved locally, the result says where, and a small text file's contents are included. It can instead be an uploaded asset's id (32 hex characters, from an 'assets' listing or an upload result), and that asset is saved to a local file. delete: the id of the one asset to remove.

paths.description: read: several published paths in place of `path`, up to 256 in one call. Each file is saved as a single `path` would be, and the result lists where each one landed, or why it could not be read, with small text files' contents included while they fit.

after.description: list with scope 'assets' only: the `next` value from a previous listing, passed to continue it.

page.description: read only: true returns the rendered page in cases where a read otherwise returns something else. A typed Artifact's read leaves out the type's own page.

capabilities.description: publish: the runtime capabilities this page declares, as {name: config}. Claude loads the `artifact-capabilities` skill before passing it. On a redeploy Claude omits the field to keep what the page has, and {} clears it.

contract.description: publish: the artifact's runtime version. Leaving it out keeps the current version (the default), 'latest' upgrades, and an exact version pins or rolls back. It changes how the published page behaves, so Claude passes it only when the author explicitly intends that change.

tools.description:

- Working directory persists between calls, but prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. No `&` needed. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.

- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.

- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

## claude-in-chrome
**IMPORTANT: If the Chrome browser tools are deferred (must be loaded via ToolSearch before use), load them with ToolSearch before calling them, and batch every tool you expect to need into ONE ToolSearch call (the select query accepts a comma-separated list). Do NOT load tools one at a time; each separate ToolSearch call wastes a full round-trip.**

Start a browser task whose tools are not yet loaded with a single call loading the core set:

Add task-specific tools to the same call when the task obviously needs them: read_console_messages / read_network_requests for debugging, form_input for forms, gif_creator for recordings, javascript_tool for page scripting. Only issue a second ToolSearch if the task later needs a tool you did not anticipate.

## claude.ai Claude Docs
Claude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai …/artifact/… link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). """SQLite store (D-016) with sqlite-vec loaded (D-018). Tables per D-021."""

import sqlite3
from pathlib import Path

import sqlite_vec

from bmw_req.config import get_settings

NOW = "(strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%fZ', 'now'))"

# Demo table set (D-021). JSON columns hold lists/objects; *_json columns are TEXT.
SCHEMA = f"""
-- Reference layer (portfolio) ------------------------------------------------
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS brand (
    id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT NOT NULL, brand_group TEXT, positioning TEXT,
    core_values_json TEXT, guardrails_json TEXT, source_ids_json TEXT
);
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS platform (
    id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, owner_brand_group TEXT, powertrains_json TEXT, introduced TEXT,
    phase_out TEXT, successor_platform_id TEXT REFERENCES platform(id), source_ids_json TEXT
);
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS vehicle_model (
    id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, brand_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES brand(id), line TEXT, body TEXT,
    segment TEXT, platform_id TEXT REFERENCES platform(id), generation TEXT, sop TEXT,
    eop_planned TEXT, powertrains_json TEXT, is_bmw_group INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1,
    market_variants_json TEXT
);
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS market (
    code TEXT PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT NOT NULL, countries_json TEXT NOT NULL,  -- ["*"] = catch-all
    climate TEXT, usage_patterns TEXT, cultural_expectations TEXT, infrastructure TEXT,
    powertrain_mix TEXT, profile_source_ids_json TEXT, profile_valid_from TEXT
);
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS plant (
    id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT NOT NULL, city TEXT, country TEXT, platforms_json TEXT,
    powertrains_json TEXT, nk_ready_from TEXT, capacity_note TEXT, source_ids_json TEXT
);
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS production (
    vehicle_model_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES vehicle_model(id), plant_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES plant(id),
    market_variant TEXT, markets_served_json TEXT, since TEXT, until TEXT, source_ids_json TEXT
);
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS sales (
    vehicle_model_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES vehicle_model(id), market_code TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES market(code),
    year INTEGER NOT NULL, units INTEGER, is_forecast INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    source_item_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES source_item(id)
);

-- Evidence layer ---------------------------------------------------------------
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS ingest_batch (
    id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, ts TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT {NOW},
    kind TEXT NOT NULL,           -- feedback_wave | study | sales | option_list | competitor_event | web_refresh | reference
    description TEXT, file TEXT
);
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS source_item (
    id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    kind TEXT NOT NULL,           -- feedback | study | sales | option_list | web | reference
    ref TEXT NOT NULL,            -- provenance: e.g. 'G60_feedback_hackathon.xlsx#Feedback_Explorer:G60-0001'
    external_id TEXT,             -- e.g. verbatim ID G60-0001
    trust_tier TEXT,              -- T1..T3
    vehicle_model_id TEXT REFERENCES vehicle_model(id), market_code TEXT REFERENCES market(code),
    country TEXT, platform_id TEXT REFERENCES platform(id),
    url TEXT, published_at TEXT, retrieved_at TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT {NOW},
    text TEXT, quote TEXT, meta_json TEXT,
    ingest_batch_id INTEGER REFERENCES ingest_batch(id),
    UNIQUE (kind, ref)
);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS ix_source_scope ON source_item(vehicle_model_id, market_code);
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS finding (
    id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, type TEXT, title TEXT NOT NULL, summary TEXT,
    scope_level TEXT,             -- derivative | platform | market | portfolio
    vehicle_model_id TEXT REFERENCES vehicle_model(id), market_code TEXT REFERENCES market(code),
    platform_id TEXT REFERENCES platform(id),
    metrics_json TEXT, created_by TEXT NOT NULL, created_at TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT {NOW}
);
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS finding_source (
    finding_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES finding(id), source_item_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES source_item(id),
    quote TEXT, relation TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'supports',   -- supports | contradicts
    PRIMARY KEY (finding_id, source_item_id)
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS verbatim_extraction (   -- one row per verbatim × extractor version (D-022)
    source_item_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES source_item(id), extractor_version TEXT NOT NULL,
    in_scope INTEGER NOT NULL, out_of_scope_reason TEXT, llm_usage_id INTEGER REFERENCES llm_usage(id),
    recheck_llm_usage_id INTEGER REFERENCES llm_usage(id),   -- second-pass check of an out-of-scope verdict (D-023)
    created_at TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT {NOW},
    PRIMARY KEY (source_item_id, extractor_version)
);
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS signal (                -- AI-extracted customer signal; input to findings (D-022)
    id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, source_item_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES source_item(id),
    extractor_version TEXT NOT NULL, category TEXT NOT NULL, topic TEXT, feedback_type TEXT NOT NULL,
    severity TEXT, need_statement TEXT, quote TEXT,
    quote_verified INTEGER NOT NULL,   -- quote is a contiguous span of the verbatim (whitespace/case normalized)
    llm_usage_id INTEGER REFERENCES llm_usage(id),   -- call (and so model) that produced it (D-023)
    FOREIGN KEY (source_item_id, extractor_version) REFERENCES verbatim_extraction(source_item_id, extractor_version)
);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS ix_signal_source ON signal(source_item_id);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS finding_signal (       -- cluster membership: which signals make up a finding (D-025)
    finding_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES finding(id), signal_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES signal(id),
    PRIMARY KEY (finding_id, signal_id)
);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS ix_finding_signal_signal ON finding_signal(signal_id);
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS study_metric (           -- one row per study item × model × market (D-026)
    id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, source_item_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES source_item(id),
    vehicle_model_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES vehicle_model(id), market_code TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES market(code),
    item TEXT NOT NULL,           -- category / question text as in the file
    scale TEXT NOT NULL,          -- mean_10 (CN/EU means) | dist_7 (US 7-point distribution)
    mean REAL, top2 REAL, bottom3 REAL, net REAL,
    z_within_column REAL,         -- standardized vs. the other items of the same model × market column
    rank_within_column INTEGER, n_items_in_column INTEGER
);

-- Decision layer ---------------------------------------------------------------
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS requirement (
    id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,          -- REQ-0001
    title TEXT NOT NULL, description TEXT, category TEXT, target_metric TEXT, acceptance_criteria TEXT,
    horizon TEXT,                 -- today | at_successor_launch
    kano_class TEXT, kano_drift TEXT, evidence_level TEXT,   -- E1..E4
    assumptions TEXT, uncertainties TEXT, conflicting_evidence TEXT,
    status TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'proposed', version INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1,
    created_at TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT {NOW}
);
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS requirement_target (
    requirement_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES requirement(id),
    vehicle_model_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES vehicle_model(id), market_code TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES market(code),
    realization TEXT,             -- carry_over | platform_wide | derivative_specific | market_variant | package
    score REAL, score_breakdown_json TEXT, priority TEXT, rationale TEXT,
    PRIMARY KEY (requirement_id, vehicle_model_id, market_code)
);
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS requirement_finding (
    requirement_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES requirement(id), finding_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES finding(id),
    relation TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'supports',
    PRIMARY KEY (requirement_id, finding_id)
);
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS fit_check (
    id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, requirement_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES requirement(id),
    vehicle_model_id TEXT REFERENCES vehicle_model(id), market_code TEXT REFERENCES market(code),
    check_type TEXT NOT NULL,     -- brand | segment | market | feasibility
    result TEXT NOT NULL,         -- pass | warn | fail
    rationale TEXT, evidence_source_ids_json TEXT, checked_by TEXT NOT NULL, checked_at TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT {NOW}
);
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS audit_event (
    id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, ts TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT {NOW},
    actor_type TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (actor_type IN ('ai', 'human', 'system')), actor_id TEXT,
    action TEXT NOT NULL, entity_type TEXT NOT NULL, entity_id TEXT NOT NULL,
    field TEXT, old_value TEXT, new_value TEXT, rationale TEXT, model TEXT, prompt_ref TEXT
);
CREATE TRIGGER IF NOT EXISTS audit_event_no_update BEFORE UPDATE ON audit_event
BEGIN SELECT RAISE(ABORT, 'audit_event is append-only'); END;
CREATE TRIGGER IF NOT EXISTS audit_event_no_delete BEFORE DELETE ON audit_event
BEGIN SELECT RAISE(ABORT, 'audit_event is append-only'); END;

-- Continuity layer (D-013) -----------------------------------------------------
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS weights_version (
    id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, weights_json TEXT NOT NULL, created_by TEXT NOT NULL,
    created_at TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT {NOW}, rationale TEXT
);
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS prioritization_run (
    id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, ts TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT {NOW},
    trigger TEXT NOT NULL,        -- new_evidence | weight_change | pm_request | scheduled
    ingest_batch_id INTEGER REFERENCES ingest_batch(id), weights_version_id INTEGER REFERENCES weights_version(id),
    model TEXT, initiated_by TEXT NOT NULL
);
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS score_snapshot (
    run_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES prioritization_run(id), requirement_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES requirement(id),
    vehicle_model_id TEXT NOT NULL, market_code TEXT NOT NULL,
    score REAL, breakdown_json TEXT, rank INTEGER, priority TEXT,
    PRIMARY KEY (run_id, requirement_id, vehicle_model_id, market_code)
);
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS change_proposal (
    id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, run_id INTEGER REFERENCES prioritization_run(id),
    requirement_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES requirement(id), vehicle_model_id TEXT, market_code TEXT,
    field TEXT NOT NULL, old_value TEXT, proposed_value TEXT, reason TEXT, evidence_delta_json TEXT,
    status TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'open',   -- open | accepted | rejected
    decided_by TEXT, decided_at TEXT, decision_rationale TEXT
);

-- LLM bookkeeping (D-014, D-010) ----------------------------------------------
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS llm_usage (
    id                 INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    created_at         TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT {NOW},
    settled_at         TEXT,
    job                TEXT NOT NULL,
    demo               INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    kind               TEXT NOT NULL,            -- responses | embeddings
    model              TEXT NOT NULL,
    service_tier       TEXT,
    status             TEXT NOT NULL,            -- reserved | completed | failed
    reserved_usd       REAL NOT NULL,
    cost_usd           REAL,
    input_tokens       INTEGER,
    cached_tokens      INTEGER,
    cache_write_tokens INTEGER,
    output_tokens      INTEGER,
    reasoning_tokens   INTEGER,
    search_calls       INTEGER,
    response_id        TEXT,
    error              TEXT
);
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS llm_cache (
    key TEXT PRIMARY KEY,         -- sha256 of model + request
    job TEXT, model TEXT NOT NULL, created_at TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT {NOW},
    output_text TEXT, llm_usage_id INTEGER REFERENCES llm_usage(id)
);

-- Vectors (D-018): rowid = source_item.id -------------------------------------
CREATE VIRTUAL TABLE IF NOT EXISTS source_embedding USING vec0(embedding float[1536]);
"""


def connect(path: Path | str | None = None) -> sqlite3.Connection:
    """Open the app DB (default `data/app.db`), load sqlite-vec and ensure the schema.

    Autocommit mode: callers open transactions explicitly (`BEGIN IMMEDIATE`).
    """
    if path is None:
        path = get_settings().db_path
    if str(path) != ":memory:":
        Path(path).parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    conn = sqlite3.connect(path, isolation_level=None, check_same_thread=False)
    conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
    conn.enable_load_extension(True)
    sqlite_vec.load(conn)
    conn.enable_load_extension(False)
    conn.execute("PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL")
    conn.execute("PRAGMA busy_timeout=10000")
    conn.execute("PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON")
    conn.executescript(SCHEMA)
    _migrate(conn)
    return conn


# Columns added after a table was first created: (table, column, definition). CREATE IF NOT EXISTS
# doesn't add them to an existing DB.
MIGRATIONS = [
    ("signal", "llm_usage_id", "INTEGER REFERENCES llm_usage(id)"),
    ("verbatim_extraction", "recheck_llm_usage_id", "INTEGER REFERENCES llm_usage(id)"),
    ("signal", "support_question", "INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0"),   # Q-020, D-024
    # Simulated ingest waves (Q-012, D-027): the wave in which an item becomes visible to the pipeline.
    ("source_item", "wave", "INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1"),
    ("finding", "source_kind", "TEXT"),            # verbatim | study | web | reference
    ("finding", "polarity", "TEXT"),               # pain | want | like | context
    ("finding", "category", "TEXT"),
    ("finding", "first_wave", "INTEGER"),
    ("requirement", "effort", "TEXT"),             # S | M | L rough effort (prioritization only, no cost math)
    ("requirement", "must_not_lose", "INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0"),
    ("requirement", "realization_note", "TEXT"),
    ("requirement", "created_by", "TEXT"),
    ("requirement", "first_run_id", "INTEGER"),
    ("requirement", "derivation_json", "TEXT"),     # raw AI draft incl. horizon_reason, cited IDs
    ("requirement_target", "evidence_level", "TEXT"),
    ("requirement_target", "proposed_priority", "TEXT"),   # AI proposal; `priority` is the PM-confirmed one
    ("requirement_target", "run_id", "INTEGER"),
    ("change_proposal", "kind", "TEXT"),            # priority | status | content | new_requirement | link_finding
    ("audit_event", "run_id", "INTEGER"),
]


def _migrate(conn: sqlite3.Connection) -> None:
    for table, column, definition in MIGRATIONS:
        cols = {r["name"] for r in conn.execute(f"PRAGMA table_info({table})")}
        if column not in cols:
            conn.execute(f"ALTER TABLE {table} ADD COLUMN {column} {definition}")
            if (table, column) == ("signal", "llm_usage_id"):
                # Backfill: until D-023 every signal came from its verbatim's first-pass call.
                conn.execute(
                    """UPDATE signal SET llm_usage_id = (SELECT e.llm_usage_id FROM verbatim_extraction e
                       WHERE e.source_item_id = signal.source_item_id AND e.extractor_version = signal.extractor_version)"""
                )
# Architecture & Workflow

**Status: DRAFT v3 — conceptual.** The workflow, entities and rules below are the agreed *concept* (D-005, D-008–D-013). The *technical* stack is decided (LangGraph, SQLite, sqlite-vec, no graph DB, Streamlit — D-015–D-020, see `tech-stack.md`). The data model below is built in SQLite (`src/bmw_req/db.py`) per D-021, with three entities folded in: `segment` → `vehicle_model.segment`, `market_profile` → columns on `market`, `finding_scope` → scope columns on `finding`. Added: `source_item.country`, `source_embedding` (sqlite-vec), `llm_cache`.

## Guiding principle

BMW decides at **portfolio level** — across shared platforms (CLAR, FAAR, Neue Klasse), plants and markets — not one car at a time. The data model is therefore **multi-brand, multi-derivative, multi-market, platform- and plant-aware from day one**. The 5 Series (G60 + China LWB G68) is the deepest worked example; F70 and G70 run through the same pipeline.

## End-to-end workflow

| # | Stage | Actor | Output |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Ingest** BMW data (feedback, study, sales, option lists) for all derivatives × markets | AI (autonomous) | `source_item` with provenance (file, sheet, row) and scope (derivative, market) |
| 2 | **Load reference data** — platforms, plants, brand positioning, segments, competitor models | AI-researched, **human-curated** | reference tables, each fact with source + date (`portfolio-reference.md`, `competitor-landscape.md` are the seeds) |
| 3 | **Enrich via web research agents** — competitors, sales, demand, reviews, trends, customer expectations (see `knowledge-base.md`) | AI (autonomous), PM can accept/reject sources | `source_item(kind=web)` with URL, date, publisher, trust tier, quote |
| 4 | **Extract signals** — classify, dedupe, cluster into findings: complaint / unmet need / must-not-lose delighter / competitor advantage / market trend / brand expectation | AI (autonomous) | `finding` with scope (derivative / platform / market / portfolio), linked sources, metrics |
| 5 | **Derive requirements** — customer-facing, actionable, measurable target + acceptance criteria; scoped to one or more derivatives × markets | AI proposes | `requirement` (status `proposed`) + `requirement_target` rows |
| 6 | **Fit & feasibility checks** per target (D-008, D-009): brand fit, segment fit, market fit, platform/plant feasibility | AI checks, flags explained | `fit_check` rows: pass / warn / fail + rationale + evidence |
| 7 | **Score & prioritize** — explainable factors incl. market volume and portfolio leverage (`requirement-model.md`) | AI computes, PM adjusts weights | score breakdown + rationale |
| 8 | **PM review** — approve / reject / edit / challenge / defer; override failed checks only with rationale | **Human (mandatory)** | status change + rationale |
| 9 | **Document & export** — requirement list, portfolio view, full audit trail | AI | JSON / XLSX export, audit timeline per requirement |

### It's a loop, not a one-shot (D-013)

The requirements process runs **~2 years**. Steps 1–9 repeat whenever something changes:

```
new ingest batch (feedback wave, study, sales update, competitor launch, web refresh)
  → re-extract / update findings (only affected ones)
  → future-need projection refresh
  → prioritization run (snapshot of all requirement-target scores & ranks)
  → change proposals (priority/status/content) → PM accepts/rejects
  → history: priority timeline per requirement with the "why" of each move
```

Triggers: `new_evidence`, `weight_change`, `pm_request`, `scheduled`. Evidence has a freshness decay; stale evidence loses weight unless re-confirmed.

### Markets are distinct customer groups (D-011)

Findings are segmented by market; every requirement-target (derivative × market) has its **own** score, priority and fit result. A `market_profile` (climate, usage, culture, infrastructure) feeds extraction, projection and fit checks. Cross-market conflicts are flagged with realization options (global / market variant / package).

### Future needs (D-012)

Step 5 includes **future-need projection**: predecessor findings + competitor trajectory + trends + market profile → need at successor SOP, with horizon (`today` / `at_successor_launch`) and Kano class + expected drift.

**Mandatory human gates:** final status of every requirement; overriding a failed brand-fit or feasibility check; accepting curated reference data (platform/plant facts). Optional gates: accepting web sources, merging/splitting findings, changing weights.

## Core data model (draft)

### Reference layer (portfolio)
```
brand(id, name, group, positioning, core_values[], guardrails_json, source_ids[])
segment(id, name, e.g. premium_compact | upper_mid | luxury, description)
platform(id e.g. CLAR | FAAR | NK, owner_brand_group, powertrains_supported[], introduced, phase_out, successor_platform_id, source_ids[])
vehicle_model(id e.g. G60, brand_id, line "5 Series", body, segment_id, platform_id, generation,
              sop, eop_planned, powertrains[], is_bmw_group, market_variants[])   -- BMW + competitors in one table
market(code EU | US | CN | RoW, countries[])
market_profile(market_code, climate, usage_patterns, cultural_expectations, infrastructure, powertrain_mix, source_ids[], valid_from)
plant(id, name, city, country, platforms_supported[], powertrains_supported[], nk_ready_from, capacity_note, source_ids[])
production(vehicle_model_id, plant_id, market_variant e.g. "G68 LWB", markets_served[], since, until)
sales(vehicle_model_id, market_code, year, units, is_forecast, source_id)
```

### Evidence layer
```
source_item(id, kind[feedback|study|sales|option_list|web|reference], trust_tier[T1..T3],
            vehicle_model_id?, market_code?, platform_id?, ref, url?, published_at?, retrieved_at,
            text, quote, meta_json)
finding(id, type, title, summary, scope_level[derivative|platform|market|portfolio],
        metrics_json, created_by, created_at)
finding_scope(finding_id, vehicle_model_id?, market_code?, platform_id?)
finding_source(finding_id, source_item_id, quote, relation[supports|contradicts])
```

### Decision layer
```
requirement(id "REQ-0001", title, description, category, target_metric, acceptance_criteria,
            horizon[today|at_successor_launch], kano_class[basic|performance|delighter], kano_drift,
            evidence_level, assumptions, uncertainties, conflicting_evidence,
            status, version)                                   -- content versioned; old versions kept
requirement_target(requirement_id, vehicle_model_id, market_code,
                   realization[carry_over|platform_wide|derivative_specific|market_variant|package],
                   score, score_breakdown_json, priority, rationale)   -- per-market priority (D-011)
requirement_finding(requirement_id, finding_id, relation[supports|contradicts])
fit_check(id, requirement_id, vehicle_model_id, market_code, check[brand|segment|market|feasibility],
          result[pass|warn|fail], rationale, evidence_source_ids[], checked_by, checked_at)
audit_event(id, ts, actor_type[ai|human|system], actor_id, action, entity_type, entity_id,
            field, old_value, new_value, rationale, model, prompt_ref)   -- append-only
```

### Continuity layer (D-013)
```
ingest_batch(id, ts, kind[feedback_wave|study|sales|competitor_event|web_refresh], description, source_ids[])
prioritization_run(id, ts, trigger[new_evidence|weight_change|pm_request|scheduled], ingest_batch_id?,
                   weights_version, model, initiated_by)
score_snapshot(run_id, requirement_id, vehicle_model_id, market_code, score, breakdown_json, rank, priority)
change_proposal(id, run_id, requirement_id, target?, field, old_value, proposed_value, reason,
                evidence_delta_json, status[open|accepted|rejected], decided_by, decided_at, decision_rationale)
weights_version(id, weights_json, created_by, created_at, rationale)
llm_usage(id, ts, job, model, status, reserved_usd, cost_usd, tokens…, search_calls)   -- budget guard (D-014)
llm_cache(key, model, output_text, llm_usage_id)   -- identical requests never re-billed (D-010)
```

Requirement IDs are global (`REQ-0001`); scope lives in `requirement_target`, so one requirement can apply to several derivatives/markets (e.g. an infotainment UX fix across all CLAR cars).

## Audit trail rules

- Append-only: no UPDATE/DELETE on `audit_event` (enforced by SQLite triggers).
- Every mutation of requirement content, targets, score, priority, evidence links, fit checks or status → one event (who/what, when, before/after, rationale).
- AI events record model name + prompt/agent version; web research events record queries and URLs.
- Access events (view/export) logged as well.

## Key UI views (planned)

- **Portfolio matrix** — derivatives × markets, with platform and plant, sales trend, top findings, requirement count.
- **Requirement detail** — evidence chain (sources → findings → requirement), fit checks, score breakdown, audit timeline, approve/reject/edit/challenge.
- **Competitor view** — per segment × market: who sells what, strengths, gaps vs. BMW.
- **Ranked backlog** — per market (EU / US / CN side by side), adjustable weights, visible re-ranking diff.
- **Priority history** — timeline per requirement across prioritization runs, each move annotated with its cause (new evidence, weight change, PM decision).
- **Change inbox** — open AI change proposals after a new ingest batch; PM accepts/rejects with rationale.
- **Market conflict view** — requirements whose priority diverges strongly between markets, with realization options.
"""Settings from the environment (.env). Model names are never hardcoded (AGENTS rule 12)."""

import os
from dataclasses import dataclass
from pathlib import Path

from dotenv import load_dotenv

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
load_dotenv(ROOT / ".env")


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Settings:
    openai_api_key: str | None
    model_fast: str
    model_smart: str
    model_embed: str
    raw_data_dir: Path
    data_dir: Path

    @property
    def db_path(self) -> Path:
        return self.data_dir / "app.db"


def _path(var: str, default: str) -> Path:
    p = Path(os.getenv(var, default))
    return p if p.is_absolute() else ROOT / p


def get_settings() -> Settings:
    return Settings(
        openai_api_key=os.getenv("OPENAI_API_KEY"),
        model_fast=os.getenv("OPENAI_MODEL_FAST", "gpt-6-luna"),
        model_smart=os.getenv("OPENAI_MODEL_SMART", "gpt-6.1-sol"),
        model_embed=os.getenv("OPENAI_MODEL_EMBED", "text-embedding-3-small"),
        raw_data_dir=_path("RAW_DATA_DIR", "challange information document/BMW-Data"),
        data_dir=_path("DATA_DIR", "data"),
    )

def connect(path: Path | str | None = None) -> sqlite3.Connection:
    """Open the app DB (default `data/app.db`), load sqlite-vec and ensure the schema.

    Autocommit mode: callers open transactions explicitly (`BEGIN IMMEDIATE`).
    """
    if path is None:
        path = get_settings().db_path
    if str(path) != ":memory:":
        Path(path).parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    conn = sqlite3.connect(path, isolation_level=None, check_same_thread=False)
    conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
    conn.enable_load_extension(True)
    sqlite_vec.load(conn)
    conn.enable_load_extension(False)
    conn.execute("PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL")
    conn.execute("PRAGMA busy_timeout=10000")
    conn.execute("PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON")
    conn.executescript(SCHEMA)
    _migrate(conn)
    return conn

    for table, column, definition in MIGRATIONS:

# Architecture & Workflow

**Status: DRAFT v3 — conceptual.** The workflow, entities and rules below are the agreed *concept* (D-005, D-008–D-013). The *technical* stack is decided (LangGraph, SQLite, sqlite-vec, no graph DB, Streamlit — D-015–D-020, see `tech-stack.md`). The data model below is built in SQLite (`src/bmw_req/db.py`) per D-021, with three entities folded in: `segment` → `vehicle_model.segment`, `market_profile` → columns on `market`, `finding_scope` → scope columns on `finding`. Added: `source_item.country`, `source_embedding` (sqlite-vec), `llm_cache`.

## Guiding principle

BMW decides at **portfolio level** — across shared platforms (CLAR, FAAR, Neue Klasse), plants and markets — not one car at a time. The data model is therefore **multi-brand, multi-derivative, multi-market, platform- and plant-aware from day one**. The 5 Series (G60 + China LWB G68) is the deepest worked example; F70 and G70 run through the same pipeline.

## End-to-end workflow

| # | Stage | Actor | Output |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Ingest** BMW data (feedback, study, sales, option lists) for all derivatives × markets | AI (autonomous) | `source_item` with provenance (file, sheet, row) and scope (derivative, market) |
| 2 | **Load reference data** — platforms, plants, brand positioning, segments, competitor models | AI-researched, **human-curated** | reference tables, each fact with source + date (`portfolio-reference.md`, `competitor-landscape.md` are the seeds) |
| 3 | **Enrich via web research agents** — competitors, sales, demand, reviews, trends, customer expectations (see `knowledge-base.md`) | AI (autonomous), PM can accept/reject sources | `source_item(kind=web)` with URL, date, publisher, trust tier, quote |
| 4 | **Extract signals** — classify, dedupe, cluster into findings: complaint / unmet need / must-not-lose delighter / competitor advantage / market trend / brand expectation | AI (autonomous) | `finding` with scope (derivative / platform / market / portfolio), linked sources, metrics |
| 5 | **Derive requirements** — customer-facing, actionable, measurable target + acceptance criteria; scoped to one or more derivatives × markets | AI proposes | `requirement` (status `proposed`) + `requirement_target` rows |
| 6 | **Fit & feasibility checks** per target (D-008, D-009): brand fit, segment fit, market fit, platform/plant feasibility | AI checks, flags explained | `fit_check` rows: pass / warn / fail + rationale + evidence |
| 7 | **Score & prioritize** — explainable factors incl. market volume and portfolio leverage (`requirement-model.md`) | AI computes, PM adjusts weights | score breakdown + rationale |
| 8 | **PM review** — approve / reject / edit / challenge / defer; override failed checks only with rationale | **Human (mandatory)** | status change + rationale |
| 9 | **Document & export** — requirement list, portfolio view, full audit trail | AI | JSON / XLSX export, audit timeline per requirement |

### It's a loop, not a one-shot (D-013)

The requirements process runs **~2 years**. Steps 1–9 repeat whenever something changes:

```
new ingest batch (feedback wave, study, sales update, competitor launch, web refresh)
  → re-extract / update findings (only affected ones)
  → future-need projection refresh
  → prioritization run (snapshot of all requirement-target scores & ranks)
  → change proposals (priority/status/content) → PM accepts/rejects
  → history: priority timeline per requirement with the "why" of each move
```

Triggers: `new_evidence`, `weight_change`, `pm_request`, `scheduled`. Evidence has a freshness decay; stale evidence loses weight unless re-confirmed.

### Markets are distinct customer groups (D-011)

Findings are segmented by market; every requirement-target (derivative × market) has its **own** score, priority and fit result. A `market_profile` (climate, usage, culture, infrastructure) feeds extraction, projection and fit checks. Cross-market conflicts are flagged with realization options (global / market variant / package).

### Future needs (D-012)

Step 5 includes **future-need projection**: predecessor findings + competitor trajectory + trends + market profile → need at successor SOP, with horizon (`today` / `at_successor_launch`) and Kano class + expected drift.

**Mandatory human gates:** final status of every requirement; overriding a failed brand-fit or feasibility check; accepting curated reference data (platform/plant facts). Optional gates: accepting web sources, merging/splitting findings, changing weights.

## Audit trail rules

- Append-only: no UPDATE/DELETE on `audit_event` (enforced by SQLite triggers).
- Every mutation of requirement content, targets, score, priority, evidence links, fit checks or status → one event (who/what, when, before/after, rationale).
- AI events record model name + prompt/agent version; web research events record queries and URLs.
- Access events (view/export) logged as well.

- **Portfolio matrix** — derivatives × markets, with platform and plant, sales trend, top findings, requirement count.
- **Requirement detail** — evidence chain (sources → findings → requirement), fit checks, score breakdown, audit timeline, approve/reject/edit/challenge.
- **Competitor view** — per segment × market: who sells what, strengths, gaps vs. BMW.
- **Ranked backlog** — per market (EU / US / CN side by side), adjustable weights, visible re-ranking diff.
- **Priority history** — timeline per requirement across prioritization runs, each move annotated with its cause (new evidence, weight change, PM decision).
- **Change inbox** — open AI change proposals after a new ingest batch; PM accepts/rejects with rationale.
- **Market conflict view** — requirements whose priority diverges strongly between markets, with realization options.

# BMW Group Portfolio Reference: Platforms, Plants, Sales

Researched on 2026-10-10. Every fact has a source and a publication date in the table rows or in the source list (S#) at the end.

Reliability tiers:
- **[BMW]**: BMW Group press release or BMW plant fact sheet. Highest confidence.
- **[Trade]**: reputable auto or trade press, such as bmwblog, electrive, just-auto or CnEVPost.
- **[Unverified]**: comes from one secondary source only, from a leak, or from my own inference. Do not quote it as fact.

Q3 2026 delivery figures were not yet published on the research date. BMW usually releases them in mid-October.

---

## 1. Platforms

BMW rarely names its platforms in official press releases. Most platform-to-model mappings below therefore rest on trade press. Plant assignments rest on BMW sources.

### 1.1 Current architectures and models

| Architecture | Drive layout / role | Current BMW/MINI models (codes) | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| **CLAR** (Cluster Architecture) | RWD/AWD, multi-energy (ICE/PHEV/BEV) | 3 Series G20/G21 (incl. M3 G80/G81), China LWB 3 Series G28 (incl. China-only BEV i3), 4 Series G22/G23/G26 + i4, 5 Series G60 / Touring G61 / China LWB G68 (incl. i5), 7 Series G70 + i7, 8 Series G14/15/16, X3 G45, China LWB X3, X4 G02 (ended Nov 2025), X5 G05, China LWB X5 G18, X6 G06, X7 G07, XM G09, Z4 G29 (ended 2026), 2 Series Coupé G42 / M2 G87, iX I20 (derivative) | [Trade] S20, S21. Codes are widely used but BMW press does not label them as "CLAR" |
| **FAAR** (successor to UKL2) | FWD/AWD, multi-energy | 1 Series F70, 2 Series Gran Coupé F74, 2 Series Active Tourer U06, X1 U11 + iX1, X2 U10 + iX2, China LWB X1/iX1, MINI Countryman U25 (ICE + BEV) | [Trade] S22, S23. **Conflict:** Wikipedia describes F70 as "UKL2", while bmwblog and others call it FAAR (an evolution of UKL). CnEVPost (S19) calls the China iX1 "CLAR", which is almost certainly wrong |
| MINI legacy UKL | FWD ICE | MINI Cooper 3-door F66, 5-door F65, Convertible F67 (Oxford) | [Unverified] codes; Oxford assignment [BMW] S16 |
| MINI / Great Wall "Spotlight" BEV | FWD BEV | MINI Cooper E/SE J01, Aceman J05 (Zhangjiagang, China; 50:50 JV with Great Wall) | [Trade] S12 |
| **Neue Klasse (NK)** — BMW's own name for the iX3 base: "new cluster architecture (NCAR)", BEV-only [BMW] AR25 p. 46 | Gen6 eDrive, 800 V, cylindrical cells, "superbrain" E/E architecture. BEV-first, but the 8th-gen 3 Series also brings NK design and tech to ICE derivatives | iX3 NA5 (since Oct 2025), i3 sedan NA0 (since Aug 2026); planned: iX3 LWB NA6 (China), i3 Touring NA1, iX4 NA7, i4 Coupé/Convertible NA2/NA3, i7 successor ND0, i1 NB0 (rumoured), NK electric X1 NB5/NB6, NK M cars (ZA0 M3, etc.) | NA5/NA0 and plants [BMW] S7, S9, S10. Codes and future list [Trade] S21 (bmwblog, 12 Dec 2025) |

### 1.2 What NK replaces, and when

- BMW says NK technology goes into **"40 new models and model updates" by 2027** [BMW] S7 (17 Sep 2025). BMW's design chief says every model will get NK design/tech [Trade] S24.
- **NK does not fully replace CLAR before roughly 2030.** The next large SUVs stay on an upgraded CLAR: X5/iX5 G65, X6/iX6 G66, X7/iX7 G67. CLAR is expected "well into the second half of the decade" [Trade] S21 (Dec 2025). **Conflict:** BMW's report lists R&D for "NEUE KLASSE models such as the BMW iX3 and the successors to the BMW X5 and the BMW 7 Series" [BMW] AR25 p. 70, 81. The X5 and G70 successors may be NK-*branded* on a CLAR-derived base (unresolved); Autocar on the next X7 [Trade] S24.
- **Mid-size BEVs move to NK first.** iX3 NA5 replaces the old CLAR iX3 G08. G08 production in China ended in March 2025 [Trade] S19. i3 NA0 replaces the CLAR electric 3 Series/i4 sedan role [Trade] S21.
- **New 3 Series (8th generation, revealed Sep 2026).** The BEV i3 is built in Munich. ICE/PHEV variants are built in Dingolfing, starting with the 320 and M350 petrol models [BMW] S11 (30 Sep 2026). Whether the ICE 3 Series sits on NK hardware or on a CLAR evolution is **[Unverified]**. BMW says the 8th-gen 3 Series "introduces Neue Klasse design and technologies".
- **China.** The China-built CLAR/FAAR BEVs (i3 LWB, i5, iX1) were reported to end production in **July 2026**. The NK iX3 LWB takes over, followed by an NK i3 LWB in early 2027 [Trade] S19 (CnEVPost, 17 Jun 2026, citing "BMW Club"). This is **[Unverified – rumour]**: the sources are a WeChat/Weibo insider relayed by CnEVPost and electrive (18 Jun 2026). BMW has not confirmed it; it only says Shenyang is "laying a solid foundation for the local production of Neue Klasse models". No later report confirms the end of production (checked 2026-10-10). The i7 was imported to China and discontinued there in June 2026 [Trade] S19.
- **FAAR replacement:** no official date. Trade press expects an NK-based electric X1 (NB5/NB6) after the current iX1 cycle, and an i1 (NB0) "toward end of decade" **[Unverified]** S21.

### 1.3 NK rollout timeline

| Model (code) | Plant | Milestone | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| iX3 (NA5) | Debrecen (HU) | Plant opened 26 Sep 2025. Series production from late Oct 2025. Second shift Feb 2026. 50,000th iX3 about 9 months after SOP (2026) | [BMW] S7, S8, S9 (BMW says only "iX3"; the code NA5 is [Trade] S21) |
| iX3 LWB (NA6) | Shenyang (BBA, CN) | Pre-series since Dec 2025. BMW says only "2026" for series production. Trade press reports SOP of 50L in Jun 2026 and launch in Q4 2026 (sources conflict). Investment ~CNY 10 bn (~EUR 1.2 bn) | [Trade] S25 (electrive, 5 Jan 2026), S19 |
| i3 sedan (NA0) | Munich (DE) | Pre-series 4 Feb 2026. Orders opened mid-Jun 2026. **SOP Aug 2026** (release dated 6 Aug 2026 says "in August"). Munich builds **BEV only from 2027** | [BMW] S10 (4 Feb 2026), S9 (6 Aug 2026) |
| 3 Series ICE/PHEV (8th gen) | Dingolfing (DE) | Revealed Sep 2026. SOP date not stated | [BMW] S11 |
| i3 + 3 Series | San Luis Potosí (MX) | NK production from 2027 (i3 and iX3 per newmobility). EUR 800 m investment, of which >EUR 500 m goes to a battery assembly centre | [BMW] S11 (says "i3 and 3er" at SLP); [Trade] S26 (Jul 2026) |
| China-specific 3 Series | Shenyang | Planned, no date | [BMW] S11 |
| i3 LWB (China) | Shenyang | "Early 2027" | [Trade] S19 |
| iX5 G65 (CLAR, not NK) | Spartanburg (US) | X5 G65 SOP Aug 2026. BMW says iX5 is the first US-built BEV "before year end" 2026. Other reports say early or late 2027 (conflict). At least 6 BEVs built in the US by 2030 | [BMW] via S27; [Trade] S27, S28 |

Gen6 supply chain: Debrecen is the first of five Gen6 battery plants [BMW] S7. Irlbach-Straßkirchen (DE) starts operating in Oct 2026, has 2 lines and makes up to 1,000 batteries per day for all German plants [BMW] S9, S13. E-motors come from Steyr (AT) [BMW] S9. Woodruff, SC supplies Spartanburg [Trade] S27.

---

## 2. Vehicle plants

The 2025 per-plant output figures are **confirmed by BMW**: BMW Group Report 2025 (AR25) p. 61, "BMW Group automobile production by plant", incl. pre-series models. They match bmwblog S14. The 2025 production programme per plant is on AR25 p. 60. BMW Group 2025 production totalled **2,456,561** vehicles (-2.3%): BMW 2,171,700, MINI 279,476, RR 5,385 [BMW] AR25 p. 12, 61.

| Plant | Country | Ownership | Models built today (codes) | Powertrains | Platform | NK conversion | Volume / capacity | Sources |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Munich** | DE | BMW | i3 NA0 (since Aug 2026). Before that: 3 Series sedan/Touring G20/G21, M3, 4 Series Gran Coupé / i4 G26 | ICE/PHEV/BEV today, **BEV-only from 2027** | CLAR → NK | First existing plant converted to NK | Up to 1,000 vehicles/day during remodelling | [BMW] S9, S13 |
| **Dingolfing** | DE | BMW | 5 Series G60/G61 + i5 + M5, 7 Series G70 + i7, 4 Series Coupé/Convertible G22/G23 + M4, iX I20. 8 Series (in the 2025 production programme [BMW] AR25 p. 60; ending in 2026, and the Apr 2026 fact sheet omits it). **Next-gen 3 Series ICE/PHEV** | ICE/PHEV/BEV on one line. BEV >25% of 2025 output, electrified >40% | CLAR (+ NK-generation 3 Series) | 7 Series LCI SOP Jul 2026 [Trade]. 3 Series ICE added 2026 | **279,553 in 2025 (-6.1%)** [BMW] AR25 p. 61; ~1,350/day, ~18,000 staff | [BMW] S13 (Jan 2026), S15 (fact sheet, Apr 2026); [Trade] S29 |
| **Regensburg** | DE | BMW | X1 U11 / iX1, X2 U10 / iX2 | ICE/PHEV/BEV | FAAR | Not announced | **356,901 in 2025 (+4.2%)**, record and highest of any European plant | [BMW] S13; [Trade] S14 |
| **Leipzig** | DE | BMW | 1 Series F70 (**exclusive**, production launch announced 1 Jul 2024, up to 500/day), 2 Series Active Tourer U06, 2 Series Gran Coupé F74, MINI Countryman U25 (incl. BEV) | ICE/PHEV/BEV | FAAR | Not announced | 4 millionth car Dec 2025. **259,430 in 2025 (+5.4%)** [BMW] AR25 p. 61 | [BMW] S13, S30 (1 Jul 2024) |
| **Debrecen** | HU | BMW | iX3 NA5 | BEV only | NK | NK from the start (first NK plant) | ~150,000/yr at full ramp-up [Trade]. 4,221 built in 2025 | [BMW] S7, S8; [Trade] S14, S31 |
| **Spartanburg** | US | BMW | X3 G45, X5 G05 → G65 (Aug 2026), X6 G06, X7 G07, XM G09, X5 M/X6 M. X4 G02 ended Nov 2025 | ICE/PHEV; BEV iX5 late 2026 or 2027 | CLAR | No NK announced. ≥6 BEVs by 2030 | **412,799 in 2025 (+4.2%), largest BMW plant** | [Trade] S14, S27, S28; [BMW] cited in S27 |

| **Shenyang Dadong** (BBA JV, BMW 75%) | CN | JV | **5 Series LWB G68 + i5 LWB** (China-only, production since Jan 2024), X3 LWB, X5 LWB G18. Old iX3 G08 for export until Mar 2025 | ICE/PHEV/BEV | CLAR | NK iX3 LWB at "Shenyang". **Which BBA site is [Unverified]** | **205,783 in 2025 (-40.2%)** | [BMW] S33 (25 Jan 2024), S34 (8 Aug 2023); [Trade] S14, S35 |
| **Shenyang Tiexi** (incl. **Lydia** section, opened 2022) | CN | JV | 1 Series (China sedan), 3 Series LWB G28, X1 LWB / iX1, X2. Lydia: i3 LWB BEV (G28 BEV, ended Jul 2026 [Trade]) | ICE/BEV | CLAR + FAAR | NK i3 LWB early 2027 [Trade] | **330,691 in 2025 (+16.4%)** | [Trade] S14, S19, S35 |

# BMW Group Portfolio Reference: Platforms, Plants, Sales

Researched on 2026-10-10. Every fact has a source and a publication date in the table rows or in the source list (S#) at the end.

Reliability tiers:
- **[BMW]**: BMW Group press release or BMW plant fact sheet. Highest confidence.
- **[Trade]**: reputable auto or trade press, such as bmwblog, electrive, just-auto or CnEVPost.
- **[Unverified]**: comes from one secondary source only, from a leak, or from my own inference. Do not quote it as fact.

Q3 2026 delivery figures were not yet published on the research date. BMW usually releases them in mid-October.

---

## 1. Platforms

BMW rarely names its platforms in official press releases. Most platform-to-model mappings below therefore rest on trade press. Plant assignments rest on BMW sources.

### 1.1 Current architectures and models

| **CLAR** (Cluster Architecture) | RWD/AWD, multi-energy (ICE/PHEV/BEV) | 3 Series G20/G21 (incl. M3 G80/G81), China LWB 3 Series G28 (incl. China-only BEV i3), 4 Series G22/G23/G26 + i4, 5 Series G60 / Touring G61 / China LWB G68 (incl. i5), 7 Series G70 + i7, 8 Series G14/15/16, X3 G45, China LWB X3, X4 G02 (ended Nov 2025), X5 G05, China LWB X5 G18, X6 G06, X7 G07, XM G09, Z4 G29 (ended 2026), 2 Series Coupé G42 / M2 G87, iX I20 (derivative) | [Trade] S20, S21. Codes are widely used but BMW press does not label them as "CLAR" |
| **FAAR** (successor to UKL2) | FWD/AWD, multi-energy | 1 Series F70, 2 Series Gran Coupé F74, 2 Series Active Tourer U06, X1 U11 + iX1, X2 U10 + iX2, China LWB X1/iX1, MINI Countryman U25 (ICE + BEV) | [Trade] S22, S23. **Conflict:** Wikipedia describes F70 as "UKL2", while bmwblog and others call it FAAR (an evolution of UKL). CnEVPost (S19) calls the China iX1 "CLAR", which is almost certainly wrong |
| MINI legacy UKL | FWD ICE | MINI Cooper 3-door F66, 5-door F65, Convertible F67 (Oxford) | [Unverified] codes; Oxford assignment [BMW] S16 |
| MINI / Great Wall "Spotlight" BEV | FWD BEV | MINI Cooper E/SE J01, Aceman J05 (Zhangjiagang, China; 50:50 JV with Great Wall) | [Trade] S12 |

BEV-first, but the 8th-gen 3 Series also brings NK design and tech to ICE derivatives | iX3 NA5 (since Oct 2025), i3 sedan NA0 (since Aug 2026); planned: iX3 LWB NA6 (China), i3 Touring NA1, iX4 NA7, i4 Coupé/Convertible NA2/NA3, i7 successor ND0, i1 NB0 (rumoured), NK electric X1 NB5/NB6, NK M cars (ZA0 M3, etc.) | NA5/NA0 and plants [BMW] S7, S9, S10. Codes and future list [Trade] S21 (bmwblog, 12 Dec 2025) |

### 1.2 What NK replaces, and when

- BMW says NK technology goes into **"40 new models and model updates" by 2027** [BMW] S7 (17 Sep 2025). BMW's design chief says every model will get NK design/tech [Trade] S24.
- **NK does not fully replace CLAR before roughly 2030.** The next large SUVs stay on an upgraded CLAR: X5/iX5 G65, X6/iX6 G66, X7/iX7 G67. CLAR is expected "well into the second half of the decade" [Trade] S21 (Dec 2025). **Conflict:** BMW's report lists R&D for "NEUE KLASSE models such as the BMW iX3 and the successors to the BMW X5 and the BMW 7 Series" [BMW] AR25 p. 70, 81. The X5 and G70 successors may be NK-*branded* on a CLAR-derived base (unresolved); Autocar on the next X7 [Trade] S24.
- **Mid-size BEVs move to NK first.** iX3 NA5 replaces the old CLAR iX3 G08. G08 production in China ended in March 2025 [Trade] S19. i3 NA0 replaces the CLAR electric 3 Series/i4 sedan role [Trade] S21.
- **New 3 Series (8th generation, revealed Sep 2026).** The BEV i3 is built in Munich. ICE/PHEV variants are built in Dingolfing, starting with the 320 and M350 petrol models [BMW] S11 (30 Sep 2026). Whether the ICE 3 Series sits on NK hardware or on a CLAR evolution is **[Unverified]**. BMW says the 8th-gen 3 Series "introduces Neue Klasse design and technologies".
- **China.** The China-built CLAR/FAAR BEVs (i3 LWB, i5, iX1) were reported to end production in **July 2026**. The NK iX3 LWB takes over, followed by an NK i3 LWB in early 2027 [Trade] S19 (CnEVPost, 17 Jun 2026, citing "BMW Club"). This is **[Unverified – rumour]**: the sources are a WeChat/Weibo insider relayed by CnEVPost and electrive (18 Jun 2026). BMW has not confirmed it; it only says Shenyang is "laying a solid foundation for the local production of Neue Klasse models". No later report confirms the end of production (checked 2026-10-10). The i7 was imported to China and discontinued there in June 2026 [Trade] S19.
- **FAAR replacement:** no official date. Trade press expects an NK-based electric X1 (NB5/NB6) after the current iX1 cycle, and an i1 (NB0) "toward end of decade" **[Unverified]** S21.

- **5 Series = Dingolfing + China LWB G68 at Dadong: CONFIRMED.** BMW press (8 Aug 2023) announced the China-only extended-wheelbase 5 Series and i5 "exclusively from China for China" at Plant Dadong, Shenyang. A 25 Jan 2024 release confirms production had started and the market launch. The wheelbase is 3,105 mm and the length 5,175 mm [Trade] (bmwblog). # Competitor Landscape, Demand Trends & Brand Fit

**Why Chinese premium brands take share from German brands in China (evidence):**

1. **Intelligent driving.** Chinese premium NEV buyers cite automated driving as the #1 purchase reason, ahead of smart cabin and styling [S54]. ADAS has up to 2× the purchase influence of Western markets, and 50% of Chinese shoppers would switch brand for better ADAS [S43]. "Insufficient intelligent driving experience" is cited for the BBA decline [S49].
2. **Smart cockpit and ecosystem.** Buyers expect phone-like UX, voice, and ecosystem integration (Huawei HarmonyOS, Xiaomi HyperOS). 45% of luxury owners say NEVs above RMB 300k need full smart connectivity [S54]. Even BMW's China Neue Klasse uses Momenta ADAS, Huawei HiCar and an Alibaba LLM [S5][S55].
3. **Brand heritage matters less.** Heritage only slightly outranks safety and handling as a premium definer, and matters less among high-income tier-1 buyers [S54][S56].
4. **Rear-seat luxury for the money.** The M9 and S800 offer zero-gravity seats, fridge, projector and 3.3 m+ wheelbases at prices below German flagships [S29][S6].
5. **Electrification gap.** "Only about 5% of BMW's sales in China are fully electric … in a market where EVs account for 46%" (Reuters, 14 Jul 2026, Global Mobility data) [S54]. Caveat: the 5% is BEV-only, while the 46% most likely counts BEV+PHEV (NEV), so the gap is overstated. EREV/PHEV options give range without anxiety [S48].
6. **Innovation over discounts.** McKinsey: steep discounts gave marginal growth, and innovation wins [S56].

### Brand-fit guardrails (for `fit_checks.brand`)

**Status: proposed (agent-written).** These rules feed a blocking gate (D-008), so a PM must review and sign them off before use. Items marked (PM judgement) are opinions, not evidence.

**All segments**
- **Fits BMW (pass):** precise steering and handling, rear-wheel-drive-biased feel and xDrive, responsive powertrains; driver-centric HMI (head-up display, Panoramic Vision, physical shortcut controls, iDrive-style haptic control); efficiency and range as "dynamics"; sporty-elegant design; M and M Performance variants; high-quality OTA and natural voice that *works*; ADAS that reduces burden while keeping the driver in charge.
- **Warn:** features that are "comfort-only" with no link to driving pleasure (acceptable but not differentiating); market-specific ecosystem partners (Huawei/Alibaba) acceptable in China only; grille-size escalation (polarising; region-specific).
- **Fail (contradicts the brand):** paywalling hardware already in the car (heated-seat precedent); touch-only access to core driving functions; soft, numb chassis tuning as default; gimmick recognition tech with no customer problem; copying the Chinese "living room on wheels" so far that the driver role is diminished in the 1 and 5 Series.

| Segment | Fits BMW (pass) | Warn | Contradicts (fail) |
|---|---|---|---|
| **1 Series** | Hot-hatch driving fun (M135), compact premium quality, intuitive physical controls, efficient BEV/PHEV option, youthful digital UX and app ecosystem | Pure value or feature stuffing to fight Chinese entrants; FWD-only perception | Cheap interior trim; touch-only climate (already criticised); losing dynamic edge vs Golf GTI |
| **5 Series / i5** | "Business athlete": dynamics plus long-distance comfort, top ADAS on the highway, fast charging and range, rear comfort in the China LWB, quiet cabin | China-only rear "boss" features in the G68 (pass for CN, warn for EU/US); third-party cockpit OS (CN only) | Sacrificing handling for float-ride everywhere; global commitment to an EREV range-extender identity **(PM judgement)** |
| **7 Series / i7** | Driver-*and*-chauffeur duality, Theatre Screen and rear lounge, Executive Lounge seats, craftsmanship, quiet BEV, L2+/L3 assisted driving | Matching Maextro/M9 gadgets one-for-one (fridge, projector) unless executed at BMW quality | Overt bling with no taste (grille-size controversy); dropping driving dynamics entirely (the S-Class owns pure comfort) |

97	**Why Chinese premium brands take share from German brands in China (evidence):**
98	
99	1. **Intelligent driving.** Chinese premium NEV buyers cite automated driving as the #1 purchase reason, ahead of smart cabin and styling [S54]. ADAS has up to 2× the purchase influence of Western markets, and 50% of Chinese shoppers would switch brand for better ADAS [S43]. "Insufficient intelligent driving experience" is cited for the BBA decline [S49].
100	2. **Smart cockpit and ecosystem.** Buyers expect phone-like UX, voice, and ecosystem integration (Huawei HarmonyOS, Xiaomi HyperOS). 45% of luxury owners say NEVs above RMB 300k need full smart connectivity [S54]. Even BMW's China Neue Klasse uses Momenta ADAS, Huawei HiCar and an Alibaba LLM [S5][S55].
101	3. **Brand heritage matters less.** Heritage only slightly outranks safety and handling as a premium definer, and matters less among high-income tier-1 buyers [S54][S56].
102	4. **Rear-seat luxury for the money.** The M9 and S800 offer zero-gravity seats, fridge, projector and 3.3 m+ wheelbases at prices below German flagships [S29][S6].
103	5. **Electrification gap.** "Only about 5% of BMW's sales in China are fully electric … in a market where EVs account for 46%" (Reuters, 14 Jul 2026, Global Mobility data) [S54]. Caveat: the 5% is BEV-only, while the 46% most likely counts BEV+PHEV (NEV), so the gap is overstated. EREV/PHEV options give range without anxiety [S48].
104	6. **Innovation over discounts.** McKinsey: steep discounts gave marginal growth, and innovation wins [S56].

# Competitor Landscape, Demand Trends & Brand Fit

**Status:** Seed v1. Researched 2026-10-10 via web search.
**Scope:** Successors of BMW 1 Series (F70), 5 Series (G60 / i5 / China LWB G68) and 7 Series (G70 / i7) in Europe (EU), China (CN) and the US.

**Conventions**
- `[S#]` refers to the source list at the end. Each source has a URL and a publication date.
- **(U)** marks something unverified: a single non-authoritative source, a figure that conflicts with another source, or general industry knowledge without a fetched source. Treat these items as evidence level E3/E4.
- Sales figures are calendar-year 2025 unless stated otherwise. Where sources disagree, both figures are shown.

---

## 0. Baseline: BMW 2025 context

| Metric | Value | Src |
|---|---|---|
| BMW Group deliveries 2025 | 2,463,681 (+0.5%); BMW brand 2,169,739 (−1.4%) — final, BMW Group Report 2025 p. 12 (S1 provisional: 2,463,715 / 2,169,761) | [S1], `bmw-annual-report-2025.md` |
| Europe (BMW + MINI) | 1,016,360 (+7.3%); BEV about 25%, BEV+PHEV over 40% | [S1] |
| China (BMW + MINI) | 625,527 (−12.5%; Q4 −15.9%), the second consecutive year of decline | [S1] |
| USA (BMW + MINI) | 417,638 (+5.0%) | [S1] |
| Group electrified share | 26% (BEV about 18%) | [S1] |
| 1 Series, Europe | 91,931 (+9.5%), #39 in Europe | [S2] |
| 5 Series, Europe, Jan–Apr 2025 | 20,402 (+56%), segment leader; i5 8,843 | [S3] |
| 5 Series, China, Jan–Nov 2025 | 107,348 (China-built, CPCA), #3 YTD among German C-segment sedans, behind A6L and E-Class (#2 in November alone). **Conflicts with BMW's `sales_volumes.xlsx`** (Q-015) | [S4] |
| i5, China, 2025 | 6,379 units. China production of i5 and iX1 reportedly ends July 2026 to make way for Neue Klasse **(U)** | [S5] |
| 7 Series, China, Dec 2025 | 1,429 units in the over-RMB-700k sedan segment (#3) | [S6] |
| 7 Series, Korea, 2025 | 5,834 (+17%), #1 among imported large sedans | [S7] |
| 7 Series, US, 2024 | 10,714 vs S-Class 8,809, Lexus LS 2,163, Audi A8 1,628 **(U, forum post)** | [S8] |
| 7 Series facelift (April 2026) | Neue-Klasse-style interior with Panoramic Vision display and 17.9″ screen, i7 ~700–728 km WLTP **(U, sources differ: 708 vs 728; BMW US gives only EPA ">350 mi")**, DC charging 195–250 kW, Alexa+-enhanced assistant from H2 2026, no L3 claim. April 2026 = reveal, SOP Jul 2026 | [S9] |

## 1. Competitor sets

### 1a. Premium compact (1 Series successor)

| **Audi A3** | EU 121,752 (+5.7%), best-selling premium model in Europe | Perceived quality, understated design, broad body styles including the sedan; China A3 still volume (5,883 in Jul 2026) | [S2][S10] |
| **Mercedes A-Class** | Global 354,795 (−5%); EU Jan–Feb 2026: 9,202 (+20%) | Badge prestige, MBUX screens, comfort. Being phased out in favour of the CLA **(U)** | [S11][S12] |
| **Mercedes CLA (new, MB.OS)** | No EU volume found **(U)** | First MB.OS car: AI assistant, OTA, up to 792 km WLTP, 320 kW DC (+325 km in 10 min). Critiques: anonymous driving feel, some cheap trim | [S13][S14] |
| **VW Golf GTI / R** (upper mainstream) | No 2025 EU figure found **(U)** | Driving fun at a lower price, hot-hatch heritage. China GTI is marginal (145 units in Jun 2026) | [S10] |
| **Volvo EX30** | Global retail 2025 98,065 (−23%) | Compact premium BEV, Scandinavian design and minimalism. Battery recall (over 40k) in 2026; withdrawn from the US | [S15][S16] |
| **Tesla Model 3 / Y** (price-adjacent) | n/a | Software, efficiency, charging network, FSD (Supervised) in the NL plus about 8 EU countries since April 2026 | [S17] |

**Why Chinese premium brands take share from German brands in China (evidence):**

1. **Intelligent driving.** Chinese premium NEV buyers cite automated driving as the #1 purchase reason, ahead of smart cabin and styling [S54]. ADAS has up to 2× the purchase influence of Western markets, and 50% of Chinese shoppers would switch brand for better ADAS [S43]. "Insufficient intelligent driving experience" is cited for the BBA decline [S49].
2. **Smart cockpit and ecosystem.** Buyers expect phone-like UX, voice, and ecosystem integration (Huawei HarmonyOS, Xiaomi HyperOS). 45% of luxury owners say NEVs above RMB 300k need full smart connectivity [S54]. Even BMW's China Neue Klasse uses Momenta ADAS, Huawei HiCar and an Alibaba LLM [S5][S55].
3. **Brand heritage matters less.** Heritage only slightly outranks safety and handling as a premium definer, and matters less among high-income tier-1 buyers [S54][S56].
4. **Rear-seat luxury for the money.** The M9 and S800 offer zero-gravity seats, fridge, projector and 3.3 m+ wheelbases at prices below German flagships [S29][S6].
5. **Electrification gap.** "Only about 5% of BMW's sales in China are fully electric … in a market where EVs account for 46%" (Reuters, 14 Jul 2026, Global Mobility data) [S54]. Caveat: the 5% is BEV-only, while the 46% most likely counts BEV+PHEV (NEV), so the gap is overstated. EREV/PHEV options give range without anxiety [S48].
6. **Innovation over discounts.** McKinsey: steep discounts gave marginal growth, and innovation wins [S56].

### Brand-fit guardrails (for `fit_checks.brand`)

**Status: proposed (agent-written).** These rules feed a blocking gate (D-008), so a PM must review and sign them off before use. Items marked (PM judgement) are opinions, not evidence.

**All segments**
- **Fits BMW (pass):** precise steering and handling, rear-wheel-drive-biased feel and xDrive, responsive powertrains; driver-centric HMI (head-up display, Panoramic Vision, physical shortcut controls, iDrive-style haptic control); efficiency and range as "dynamics"; sporty-elegant design; M and M Performance variants; high-quality OTA and natural voice that *works*; ADAS that reduces burden while keeping the driver in charge.
- **Warn:** features that are "comfort-only" with no link to driving pleasure (acceptable but not differentiating); market-specific ecosystem partners (Huawei/Alibaba) acceptable in China only; grille-size escalation (polarising; region-specific).
- **Fail (contradicts the brand):** paywalling hardware already in the car (heated-seat precedent); touch-only access to core driving functions; soft, numb chassis tuning as default; gimmick recognition tech with no customer problem; copying the Chinese "living room on wheels" so far that the driver role is diminished in the 1 and 5 Series.

| Segment | Fits BMW (pass) | Warn | Contradicts (fail) |
|---|---|---|---|
| **1 Series** | Hot-hatch driving fun (M135), compact premium quality, intuitive physical controls, efficient BEV/PHEV option, youthful digital UX and app ecosystem | Pure value or feature stuffing to fight Chinese entrants; FWD-only perception | Cheap interior trim; touch-only climate (already criticised); losing dynamic edge vs Golf GTI |
| **5 Series / i5** | "Business athlete": dynamics plus long-distance comfort, top ADAS on the highway, fast charging and range, rear comfort in the China LWB, quiet cabin | China-only rear "boss" features in the G68 (pass for CN, warn for EU/US); third-party cockpit OS (CN only) | Sacrificing handling for float-ride everywhere; global commitment to an EREV range-extender identity **(PM judgement)** |
| **7 Series / i7** | Driver-*and*-chauffeur duality, Theatre Screen and rear lounge, Executive Lounge seats, craftsmanship, quiet BEV, L2+/L3 assisted driving | Matching Maextro/M9 gadgets one-for-one (fridge, projector) unless executed at BMW quality | Overt bling with no taste (grille-size controversy); dropping driving dynamics entirely (the S-Class owns pure comfort) |
