"""Verbatim signal extraction (luna, structured output). v2 = Q-018 fixes after the D-014 pilot;
v3 = one consistent scope rule for mixed verbatims and support-call questions (Q-020, D-024)."""

import json
import re
from typing import Literal

from pydantic import BaseModel, Field

from bmw_req.llm import LLM

EXTRACTOR_VERSION = "extract-v3"

Category = Literal[
    "Exterior", "Interior", "Comfort & Space", "Infotainment & Digital", "Driving Experience",
    "Powertrain (as experienced)", "Range & Charging", "Driver Assistance (as experienced)",
    "Variants & Packages", "Design & Quality Perception",
]


class Signal(BaseModel):
    category: Category
    topic: str = Field(description="Short component/topic, e.g. 'Touch screen', 'Rear seat legroom'")
    feedback_type: Literal["like", "defect", "difficult_to_use", "complaint", "want"]
    severity: Literal["low", "medium", "high"]
    need_statement: str = Field(description="The underlying customer need, solution-neutral, one sentence")
    quote: str = Field(description="Exact substring of the verbatim that supports this signal")
    support_question: bool = Field(
        description="True if the signal only shows the customer needed help or asked how a function works"
    )
"""OpenAI list prices in USD per 1M tokens (D-014, checked 2026-10-10 on
developers.openai.com/api/docs/pricing). A model missing here is refused by the guard."""

from dataclasses import dataclass


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Price:
    input: float
    cached_input: float
    output: float


PRICES: dict[str, Price] = {
    "gpt-6-luna": Price(input=0.10, cached_input=0.01, output=0.50),
    "gpt-6.1-sol": Price(input=2.00, cached_input=0.10, output=10.00),
    "text-embedding-3-small": Price(input=0.02, cached_input=0.02, output=0.0),
}

FLEX_FACTOR = 0.5            # Flex = Batch = -50%
CACHE_WRITE_FACTOR = 1.25    # cache writes cost 1.25x input
WEB_SEARCH_PER_CALL = 10.0 / 1000
# D-014 web-research assumption: ~20k content tokens per billed search call (input rate).
WEB_SEARCH_CONTENT_TOKENS = 20_000

entries.name: WebFetch
entries.description:
Fetches a URL, converts the page to markdown, and answers `prompt` against it using a small fast model.

- Fails on authenticated/private URLs — use an authenticated MCP tool or `gh` for those instead. claude.ai artifact links (claude.ai/artifact/{id} or claude.ai/code/artifact/{uuid}) are published artifacts: read them with the Artifact tool (action "read"), not WebFetch or curl.
- Fails on localhost and other hostnames without a dot; for a local server, use curl via Bash.
- HTTP is upgraded to HTTPS. Cross-host redirects are returned to you rather than followed; call again with the redirect URL.
- Responses are cached for 15 minutes per URL.

url.description: The URL to fetch content from

prompt.description: The prompt to run on the fetched content

offset.description: Character position in the page text to start reading from. Use it to read on through a page too long for one call, with the value the previous result gave.

entries.name: WebSearch
entries.description:
Search the web. Returns result blocks with titles and URLs. US-only.

- The current month is (provided in the conversation below) — use this when searching for recent information.
- `allowed_domains` / `blocked_domains` filter results.
- After answering from results, end with a "Sources:" list of the URLs you used as markdown links.

allowed_domains.description: Only include search results from these domains

blocked_domains.description: Never include search results from these domains

mode.description: "standard": the normal web search: quick and cheap; right for straightforward lookups (reference facts, official pages, documentation, well-known people, places and topics) and simple follow-up lookups. "extended": a thorough, fresh search at several times the cost and latency.

The most authoritative figure for January 2025 comes from the Congressional Research Service, which relies on DOE's Alternative Fuels Data Center (AFDC). It counted 75,107 public charging stations available across the United States, with a total of 207,227 charging ports, including temporarily unavailable stations. Of those ports, 155,162 were Level 2 and 51,193 were DC fast.

Later AFDC-based counts are higher. One report says the US has passed 250,000 public EV charging ports, with 250,406 individual charging hookups across 80,543 station locations. That report is dated June 2026, so it is more recent than the 2025 figures. I could not confirm that total against AFDC directly.

Some figures in the results are not directly comparable. A October 2025 snapshot counted 170,033 public AC Level 2 ports, which excludes DC fast chargers. Another source, GreenCars, gives rough early-2025 estimates of over 180,000 public charging ports nationwide, which is looser than the CRS count. For a 2025 AFDC total, the CRS January 2025 figure of 207,227 is the best-supported number in these results.

Ideal Conditions","url":"https://insideevs.com/news/704318/ev-winter-range-loss-vs-ideal-conditions/"},{"title":"EVs Lose 30% Of Their Range On Average In The Winter Vs. Ideal Conditions","url":"https://insideevs.com/news/704318/ev-winter-range-loss-vs-ideal-conditions/about:blank"},{"title":"Sustainable Business News (SBIZ)","url":"https://sustainablebiz.ca/evs-lose-up-to-39-of-range-in-cold-weather-tests-caa"}]

Recurrent has published several winter range studies, and their headline numbers differ because the test conditions and vehicle sets vary.

- **Freezing-temperature report (16 to 46%):** Freezing temperatures can lower the range of battery electric vehicles by 16-46% depending on the make, model and year. The Audi e-tron had the smallest loss at 16%, and the VW ID.4 had the largest at 46%.
- **About 30% average at 32°F:** A later analysis of over 10,000 EVs found drops averaging roughly 30% at 32°F compared with ideal conditions, with Tesla models showing the largest drops relative to EPA figures (EVs lose about 30% of their range on average when driving at 32 degrees Fahrenheit compared to ideal conditions).
- **About 20% average at 0°C or below:** A study based on over 18,000 EVs reported that EVs lose an average of 20% of their range when temperatures hit 0°C or lower. It also found the Tesla Model X retaining 89% of its range in freezing conditions.
- **Up to 35% in 20 to 30°F:** One study of about 7,000 EVs found that on average, they found EVs can lose as much as 35% percent of their range in this level of cold, while others can lose as little as 3%.
- **Winter road test (30% average):** Recurrent's road tests of 18 models found battery range was cut by 30 per cent on average.

Across these studies, the cold-weather loss is commonly summarized as roughly 20 to 30% on average, with a wide spread between models. Heat pumps help: one report noted that both models benefited from using an efficient heat pump for their climate control systems, which redistributes heat being generated by the powertrain. Recurrent also says the loss is temporary, since the range loss is temporary and does no long-term damage to the battery.

Public charging points in China reached about 4.7 million at the end of 2025, with total charging points near 20 million. The sources below are news reports citing EVCIPA and the National Energy Administration (NEA), and their figures differ slightly by source and date.

- **End of 2025:** One report gives a total of 20.092 million charging points, including 4.717 million public and 15.375 million private, citing NEA data. As of the end of December 2025, China had a total of 20.092 million electric vehicle (EV) charging points nationwide, an increase of 49.7% year-on-year. This includes 4.717 million public chargers and 15.375 million private chargers.
- **November 2025:** The China Charging Alliance reported 19.322 million total charging infrastructure (guns), an increase of 52.0% over the previous year. Among them, there were 4.625 million public charging facilities (guns).
- **Mid-2025 (EVCIPA):** As of June, total charging points reached 16.1 million units. Among them, there were 4.096 million public charging facilities (guns).
- **End of February 2026 (latest found):** Total charging points reached 21.01 million by the end of February 2026, up 47.8 percent year on year, according to the National Energy Administration. Of this total, public charging facilities numbered 4.834 million.
- **Targets:** In October 2025, China unveiled a three-year action plan aiming to establish a nationwide network of 28 million charging facilities, with public charging capacity surpassing 300 million kilowatts by the end of 2027.

Caveats: "charging points," "facilities," and "guns" are used interchangeably across sources, and I did not find an official EVCIPA year-end 2025 release, so the 20.092 million / 4.717 million figures come from a single secondary report. The end-2024 base was 12.82 million total, per EVCIPA data reported by Argus.

- **End of 2025:** One report gives a total of 20.092 million charging points, including 4.717 million public and 15.375 million private, citing NEA data. As of the end of December 2025, China had a total of 20.092 million electric vehicle (EV) charging points nationwide, an increase of 49.7% year-on-year. This includes 4.717 million public chargers and 15.375 million private chargers.
- **November 2025:** The China Charging Alliance reported 19.322 million total charging infrastructure (guns), an increase of 52.0% over the previous year. Among them, there were 4.625 million public charging facilities (guns).
- **Mid-2025 (EVCIPA):** As of June, total charging points reached 16.1 million units. Among them, there were 4.096 million public charging facilities (guns).
- **End of February 2026 (latest found):** Total charging points reached 21.01 million by the end of February 2026, up 47.8 percent year on year, according to the National Energy Administration. Of this total, public charging facilities numbered 4.834 million.
- **Targets:** In October 2025, China unveiled a three-year action plan aiming to establish a nationwide network of 28 million charging facilities, with public charging capacity surpassing 300 million kilowatts by the end of 2027.

Caveats: "charging points," "facilities," and "guns" are used interchangeably across sources, and I did not find an official EVCIPA year-end 2025 release, so the 20.092 million / 4.717 million figures come from a single secondary report. The end-2024 base was 12.82 million total, per EVCIPA data reported by Argus.

The FHWA's own age-and-sex table gives a total average of about 13,476 miles per driver per year, but the year isn't stated on the page. Secondary sources cite newer figures, so the number depends on the year and the source.

- **FHWA table:** The FHWA's Office of Highway Policy Information breaks out annual miles per driver by age and sex. The total average is 13,476, with men at 16,550 and women at 10,142 Average Annual Miles per Driver by Age Group.
- **2022 figure:** Insurify attributes a 2022 average of 13,482 miles to FHWA data The average American drove 13,482 miles in 2022, according to the U.S. Department of Transportation's Federal Highway Administration (FHWA).
- **Other figures:** MoneyGeek cites 13,596 miles as the FHWA average for U.S. drivers The average annual mileage for U.S. drivers is 13,596 miles, or about 37 miles a day and 1,133 miles a month, according to the Federal Highway Administration (FHWA).
- **2023 figure:** CarCheckerVIN, a vehicle-history vendor, reports 13,662 miles per licensed driver using FHWA Highway Statistics 2023 and notes that this is distinct from its 11,106-mile per-vehicle figure Because 13,662 is miles per licensed driver, not per vehicle. I could not confirm this against FHWA's own publication.

Recommendation: For a citable national figure, go to FHWA's Highway Statistics tables (VM-1 and the driver-based tables) directly. The search results don't include the official 2023 driver table, so the 13,476 table figure should be treated as undated, and the 2022 and 2023 numbers come from secondary sources.

tokens_usd = (
        uncached * p.input
        + cached_tokens * p.cached_input
        + cache_write_tokens * p.input * CACHE_WRITE_FACTOR
        + output_tokens * p.output
    ) / 1e6
    if flex:
        tokens_usd *= FLEX_FACTOR
    return tokens_usd + search_calls * WEB_SEARCH_PER_CALL


def spent_usd(conn: sqlite3.Connection) -> float:
    return conn.execute("SELECT COALESCE(SUM(cost_usd), 0) FROM llm_usage WHERE status != 'reserved'").fetchone()[0]


def committed_usd(conn: sqlite3.Connection) -> float:
    return conn.execute(
        "SELECT COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN status = 'reserved' THEN reserved_usd ELSE cost_usd END), 0) FROM llm_usage"
    ).fetchone()[0]


def reserve(conn: sqlite3.Connection, *, job: str, kind: str, model: str, reserved_usd: float, demo: bool) -> int:
    """Insert a reservation row, or raise BudgetExceeded if it would cross a threshold."""
    conn.execute("BEGIN IMMEDIATE")
    try:
        after = committed_usd(conn) + reserved_usd
        if after > HARD_STOP_USD:
            raise BudgetExceeded(f"Hard stop: ${after:.2f} would exceed ${HARD_STOP_USD:.0f} ({job})")
        if not demo and after > BLOCK_NON_DEMO_USD:
            raise BudgetExceeded(f"Non-demo jobs blocked: ${after:.2f} would exceed ${BLOCK_NON_DEMO_USD:.0f} ({job})")
        cur = conn.execute(
            "INSERT INTO llm_usage (job, demo, kind, model, status, reserved_usd) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, 'reserved', ?)",
            (job, int(demo), kind, model, reserved_usd),
        )
        conn.execute("COMMIT")
    except BaseException:
        conn.execute("ROLLBACK")
        raise
    if after > WARN_USD:
        log.warning("LLM spend warning: committed $%.2f > $%.0f — re-estimate the plan (D-014)", after, WARN_USD)
    return cur.lastrowid


def settle(conn: sqlite3.Connection, usage_id: int, *, status: str, cost_usd: float, **fields) -> None:
    """Replace a reservation with actual usage. `fields` are llm_usage columns (tokens, response_id, error, ...)."""
    cols = ["status", "cost_usd", *fields]
    sets = ", ".join(f"{c} = ?" for c in cols)
    conn.execute(
        f"UPDATE llm_usage SET {sets}, settled_at = strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%fZ', 'now') WHERE id = ?",
        (status, cost_usd, *fields.values(), usage_id),
    )
"""D-014 pilot: 50 G60 US verbatims (luna) → 5 requirements (sol). Measures real tokens and cost.

Usage: uv run python scripts/pilot.py   — results in data/pilot/. Aborts if pilot spend would pass PILOT_CAP_USD.
"""

import json
import random
import sys
import time
from pathlib import Path

from bmw_req.config import get_settings
from bmw_req.db import connect
from bmw_req.llm import LLM, budget
from bmw_req.pipeline.derive import check_derivation, derive
from bmw_req.pipeline.extract import check_batch, extract_batch

SEED = 42
PER_CHANNEL = {"Source B": 20, "Source A": 10, "Source C": 10, "Source D": 10}
BATCH_SIZE = 25
PILOT_CAP_USD = 1.00
JOB = "pilot"


def spend_line(conn, start):
    return f"pilot so far ${budget.committed_usd(conn) - start:.4f} | total committed ${budget.committed_usd(conn):.4f}"


def main():
    out = get_settings().data_dir / "pilot"
    out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    conn = connect()
    llm = LLM(conn=conn)
    start = budget.committed_usd(conn)
    print(f"start: total committed ${start:.4f}")

    rng = random.Random(SEED)
    sample = []
    for channel, n in PER_CHANNEL.items():
        rows = conn.execute(
            "SELECT external_id, text, meta_json FROM source_item WHERE vehicle_model_id = 'G60' AND market_code = 'US' "
            "AND json_extract(meta_json, '$.channel') = ? ORDER BY external_id", (channel,)
        ).fetchall()
        for r in rng.sample(rows, n):
            meta = json.loads(r["meta_json"])
            sample.append({"id": r["external_id"], "text": r["text"], "engine": meta["engine"],
                           "channel": channel, "bmw_labels": meta["bmw_labels"]})
    rng.shuffle(sample)

    batches, all_results = [], []
    for i in range(0, len(sample), BATCH_SIZE):
        chunk = sample[i:i + BATCH_SIZE]
        if budget.committed_usd(conn) - start > PILOT_CAP_USD:
            sys.exit(f"ABORT: pilot cap ${PILOT_CAP_USD} reached")
        t0 = time.time()
        parsed, res = extract_batch(llm, chunk, job=f"{JOB}:extract")
        checks = check_batch(chunk, parsed)
        print(f"extract batch {i // BATCH_SIZE + 1}: {time.time() - t0:.0f}s, ${res.cost_usd:.4f}, "
              f"tier={getattr(res.response, 'service_tier', None)}, cached={res.cached}, checks={checks}")
        print("  " + spend_line(conn, start))
        batches.append({"usage_id": res.usage_id, "cost_usd": res.cost_usd, "checks": checks})
        all_results += [r.model_dump() for r in parsed.results]

    (out / "sample.json").write_text(json.dumps(sample, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False))
    (out / "extraction.json").write_text(json.dumps(all_results, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False))

    signals = [{"verbatim_id": r["verbatim_id"], **s} for r in all_results for s in r["signals"]]
    if budget.committed_usd(conn) - start > PILOT_CAP_USD:
        sys.exit(f"ABORT: pilot cap ${PILOT_CAP_USD} reached")
    t0 = time.time()
    context = {"derivative": "G60 (BMW 5 Series sedan, incl. i5)", "market": "US", "segment": "premium upper-mid-size",
               "evidence_base": f"{len(sample)} sampled verbatims (pilot)"}
    parsed, res = derive(llm, context, signals, n=5, job=f"{JOB}:derive")
    checks = check_derivation(parsed, {v["id"] for v in sample})
    print(f"derive: {time.time() - t0:.0f}s, ${res.cost_usd:.4f}, tier={getattr(res.response, 'service_tier', None)}, "
          f"cached={res.cached}, checks={checks}")
    print("  " + spend_line(conn, start))
    (out / "requirements.json").write_text(json.dumps(parsed.model_dump(), indent=2, ensure_ascii=False))
    print(f"done: {spend_line(conn, start)}")

"""`uv run python -m bmw_req.ingest [F70 G60 G70]` — seed reference rows and ingest feedback files."""

import sys

from bmw_req.config import get_settings
from bmw_req.db import connect
from bmw_req.ingest import reference
from bmw_req.ingest.feedback import ingest_feedback


def main(derivatives: list[str]) -> None:
    settings = get_settings()
    conn = connect()
    reference.seed(conn)
    for d in derivatives:
        n = ingest_feedback(conn, settings.raw_data_dir / f"{d}_feedback_hackathon.xlsx")
        print(f"{d}: {n} new verbatims")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main(sys.argv[1:] or ["G60"])

# --- Curated reference layer (knowledge-base.md layer 2) --------------------------------------------------

def _j(v):
    return None if v is None else json.dumps(v, ensure_ascii=False, sort_keys=True)


def load_reference(conn: sqlite3.Connection) -> dict:
    """Load `bmw_req.reference_data` idempotently: sources → source_item(kind='reference'), then platforms,
    plants, production, brands, vehicle models (BMW + competitors) and market profiles, each pointing at the
    source_item ids. Writes one audit_event (actor 'system', action 'load_reference') when content changed."""
    import hashlib

    from bmw_req import reference_data as rd

    payload = {k: getattr(rd, k) for k in ("SOURCES", "PLATFORMS", "PLANTS", "PRODUCTION", "BRANDS",
                                           "BMW_MODELS", "COMPETITOR_MODELS", "MARKET_PROFILES")}
    digest = hashlib.sha1(json.dumps(payload, sort_keys=True, default=str).encode()).hexdigest()[:16]
    last = conn.execute("SELECT new_value FROM audit_event WHERE action = 'load_reference' ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT 1").fetchone()
    seed(conn)
    conn.execute("BEGIN IMMEDIATE")
    try:
        batch = conn.execute("SELECT id FROM ingest_batch WHERE kind = 'reference' AND description = ?",
                             (f"curated reference layer {digest}",)).fetchone()
        batch_id = batch["id"] if batch else conn.execute(
            "INSERT INTO ingest_batch (kind, description, file) VALUES ('reference', ?, 'src/bmw_req/reference_data.py')",
            (f"curated reference layer {digest}",)).lastrowid
        ids = {}
        for key, (ref, url, published, tier, text, unverified) in rd.SOURCES.items():
            meta = _j({"key": key, "unverified": unverified, "origin_doc": ref.split("#")[0]})
            conn.execute(
                """INSERT INTO source_item (kind, ref, external_id, trust_tier, url, published_at, text, meta_json, ingest_batch_id)
                   VALUES ('reference', ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)
                   ON CONFLICT(kind, ref) DO UPDATE SET external_id=excluded.external_id, trust_tier=excluded.trust_tier,
                     url=excluded.url, published_at=excluded.published_at, text=excluded.text, meta_json=excluded.meta_json""",
                (ref, key, tier, url, published, text, meta, batch_id))
            ids[key] = conn.execute("SELECT id FROM source_item WHERE kind = 'reference' AND ref = ?", (ref,)).fetchone()["id"]

        def sids(keys):
            missing = [k for k in keys if k not in ids]
            if missing:
                raise KeyError(f"unknown reference source keys: {missing}")
            return _j([ids[k] for k in keys])

        for pid, owner, pts, intro, out, succ, src in rd.PLATFORMS:
            conn.execute(
                """INSERT INTO platform (id, owner_brand_group, powertrains_json, introduced, phase_out, successor_platform_id, source_ids_json)
                   VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, NULL, ?) ON CONFLICT(id) DO UPDATE SET owner_brand_group=excluded.owner_brand_group,
                   powertrains_json=excluded.powertrains_json, introduced=excluded.introduced, phase_out=excluded.phase_out,
                   source_ids_json=excluded.source_ids_json""",
                (pid, owner, _j(pts), intro, out, sids(src)))
        for pid, *_rest in rd.PLATFORMS:
            conn.execute("UPDATE platform SET successor_platform_id = ? WHERE id = ?", (_rest[4], pid))

        for pid, name, city, country, plats, pts, nk, cap, src in rd.PLANTS:
            conn.execute(
                """INSERT INTO plant (id, name, city, country, platforms_json, powertrains_json, nk_ready_from, capacity_note, source_ids_json)
                   VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?) ON CONFLICT(id) DO UPDATE SET name=excluded.name, city=excluded.city,
                   country=excluded.country, platforms_json=excluded.platforms_json, powertrains_json=excluded.powertrains_json,
                   nk_ready_from=excluded.nk_ready_from, capacity_note=excluded.capacity_note, source_ids_json=excluded.source_ids_json""",
                (pid, name, city, country, _j(plats), _j(pts), nk, cap, sids(src)))

        for bid, name, group, pos, values, guard, src in rd.BRANDS:
            conn.execute(
                """INSERT INTO brand (id, name, brand_group, positioning, core_values_json, guardrails_json, source_ids_json)
                   VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?) ON CONFLICT(id) DO UPDATE SET name=excluded.name, brand_group=excluded.brand_group,
                   positioning=excluded.positioning, core_values_json=excluded.core_values_json,
                   guardrails_json=excluded.guardrails_json, source_ids_json=excluded.source_ids_json""",
                (bid, name, group, pos, _j(values), _j(guard), sids(src)))

        for mid, f in rd.BMW_MODELS.items():
            conn.execute(
                """UPDATE vehicle_model SET segment=?, platform_id=?, generation=?, sop=?, powertrains_json=?,
                   market_variants_json=?, profile_json=?, source_ids_json=?, is_bmw_group=1 WHERE id=?""",
                (f["segment"], f["platform_id"], f["generation"], f["sop"], _j(f["powertrains"]),
                 _j(f["market_variants"]), _j(f["profile"]), sids(f["sources"]), mid))
        for mid, brand, line, body, seg, pts, vs, markets, prof, src in rd.COMPETITOR_MODELS:
            conn.execute(
                """INSERT INTO vehicle_model (id, brand_id, line, body, segment, powertrains_json, is_bmw_group, profile_json, source_ids_json)
                   VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, 0, ?, ?) ON CONFLICT(id) DO UPDATE SET brand_id=excluded.brand_id, line=excluded.line,
                   body=excluded.body, segment=excluded.segment, powertrains_json=excluded.powertrains_json, is_bmw_group=0,
                   profile_json=excluded.profile_json, source_ids_json=excluded.source_ids_json""",
                (mid, brand, line, body, seg, _j(pts), _j({**prof, "competes_with": vs, "markets": markets}), sids(src)))

        conn.execute("DELETE FROM production WHERE vehicle_model_id IN (%s)" % ",".join("?" * len(rd.BMW_MODELS)),
                     list(rd.BMW_MODELS))
        for mid, plant, variant, markets, since, until, src in rd.PRODUCTION:
            conn.execute(
                """INSERT INTO production (vehicle_model_id, plant_id, market_variant, markets_served_json, since, until, source_ids_json)
                   VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)""", (mid, plant, variant, _j(markets), since, until, sids(src)))

        for code, p in rd.MARKET_PROFILES.items():
            conn.execute(
                """UPDATE market SET climate=?, usage_patterns=?, cultural_expectations=?, infrastructure=?, powertrain_mix=?,
                   profile_source_ids_json=?, profile_valid_from='2026-10-10' WHERE code=?""",
                (p["climate"], p["usage_patterns"], p["cultural_expectations"], p["infrastructure"], p["powertrain_mix"],
                 sids(p["sources"]), code))

        counts = {"sources": len(rd.SOURCES), "platforms": len(rd.PLATFORMS), "plants": len(rd.PLANTS),
                  "production": len(rd.PRODUCTION), "brands": len(rd.BRANDS), "bmw_models": len(rd.BMW_MODELS),
                  "competitor_models": len(rd.COMPETITOR_MODELS), "market_profiles": len(rd.MARKET_PROFILES)}
        changed = last is None or json.loads(last["new_value"]).get("digest") != digest
        if changed:
            conn.execute(
                """INSERT INTO audit_event (actor_type, actor_id, action, entity_type, entity_id, old_value, new_value, rationale)
                   VALUES ('system', 'ingest.reference', 'load_reference', 'reference_layer', 'reference_data', ?, ?, ?)""",
                (last["new_value"] if last else None, _j({"digest": digest, **counts}),
                 "Curated reference layer loaded from cited seed docs; status proposed - PM must accept reference facts and brand guardrails."))
        conn.execute("COMMIT")
    except BaseException:
        conn.execute("ROLLBACK")
        raise
    return {**counts, "changed": changed}


if __name__ == "__main__":
    from bmw_req.db import connect

    print(load_reference(connect()))

"""Research plan as data: vehicle lines × markets × agents (knowledge-base.md). Wave-3 tasks simulate
'market events' — new information that arrives later in the multi-wave process (Q-012, D-027)."""

from bmw_req.research.agents import Task

# (line, derivative, market, main rivals in that market, BMW model name for reviews)
LINE_MARKETS = [
    ("5 Series", "G60", "US", "Mercedes E-Class, Audi A6 e-tron, Lexus ES, Genesis G80, Tesla Model 3", "BMW 5 Series / i5"),
    ("5 Series", "G60", "EU", "Mercedes E-Class, Audi A6 / A6 e-tron, Tesla Model 3", "BMW 5 Series / i5"),
    ("5 Series", "G68", "CN", "Mercedes E-Class L, Audi A6L, Xiaomi SU7, Tesla Model 3, NIO ET5/ET7, AITO", "BMW 5 Series long wheelbase (5 Series Li / i5 LWB)"),
    ("7 Series", "G70", "US", "Mercedes S-Class, Lexus LS, Porsche Panamera, Audi A8", "BMW 7 Series / i7"),
    ("7 Series", "G70", "CN", "Mercedes S-Class / Maybach S, Maextro S800, AITO M9, Yangwang U7, Audi A8L", "BMW 7 Series / i7"),
    ("7 Series", "G70", "EU", "Mercedes S-Class / EQS, Audi A8, Porsche Panamera", "BMW 7 Series / i7"),
    ("1 Series", "F70", "EU", "Audi A3, Mercedes A-Class / CLA, VW Golf GTI, Volvo EX30", "BMW 1 Series (F70)"),
    ("1 Series", "F70", "RoW", "Audi A3, Mercedes A-Class / CLA, VW Golf GTI (Japan, UK-adjacent markets)", "BMW 1 Series (F70)"),
]

TREND_FOCUS = ("software and AI voice assistant, ADAS experience, charging/range, interior and rear-seat comfort, "
               "physical vs touch controls, personalisation")


def _slug(*parts) -> str:
    return ":".join(p for p in parts if p)


def build_plan() -> list[Task]:
    tasks: list[Task] = []
    for line, d, m, rivals, bmw_name in LINE_MARKETS:
        ctx = {"Main rivals": rivals}
        tasks.append(Task(_slug("cs", d, m), "competitor_scout", line, d, m,
                          f"What do {rivals} offer customers in {m} in 2025-2026 that the {bmw_name} lacks or does worse?", context=ctx))
        tasks.append(Task(_slug("rm", d, m), "review_miner", line, d, m,
                          f"Professional reviews (2024-2026) of the {bmw_name} and its main rival(s) ({rivals}) in {m}: "
                          "praise and criticism on interior, infotainment/iDrive, comfort, driving, ADAS, range/charging.", context=ctx))
        tasks.append(Task(_slug("ts", d, m), "trend_scout", line, d, m,
                          f"What will premium {'compact' if line == '1 Series' else 'luxury' if line == '7 Series' else 'executive-sedan'} "
                          f"buyers in {m} expect by 2029-2031: {TREND_FOCUS}."))
    # deepest line (5 Series) gets an extra competitor angle per market and a sales analyst
    tasks += [
        Task("cs2:G68:CN", "competitor_scout", "5 Series", "G68", "CN",
             "Chinese premium EV/EREV sedans and SUVs (Xiaomi SU7/YU7, AITO, Zeekr, NIO): smart cockpit, Huawei/HarmonyOS ecosystem, "
             "intelligent driving (city NOA), rear-seat features that draw buyers away from German executive sedans."),
        Task("cs2:G60:US", "competitor_scout", "5 Series", "G60", "US",
             "Driver assistance (hands-free highway driving such as Super Cruise / BlueCruise / Tesla FSD), connectivity and "
             "reliability that US midsize-luxury buyers value in rivals of the BMW 5 Series."),
        Task("cs2:G60:EU", "competitor_scout", "5 Series", "G60", "EU",
             "New Mercedes CLA/E-Class MB.OS and Audi A6 e-tron features in Europe: AI assistant, charging speed, range, OTA updates."),
        Task("ma:G68:CN", "market_analyst", "5 Series", "G68", "CN",
             "Sales and growth of executive sedans (BMW 5 Series LWB, Audi A6L, Mercedes E-Class L) and new-energy rivals in China 2025-2026."),
        Task("ma:G60:EU", "market_analyst", "5 Series", "G60", "EU",
             "Executive sedan and wagon sales in Europe 2025-2026 (BMW 5 Series/i5, Mercedes E-Class, Audi A6) and BEV share."),
        Task("ma:G60:US", "market_analyst", "5 Series", "G60", "US",
             "US midsize luxury sedan sales 2025-2026 and EV demand after the federal tax credit ended."),
        Task("ma:G70:CN", "market_analyst", "7 Series", "G70", "CN",
             "China ultra-luxury sedan sales 2025-2026 (Maextro S800, BMW 7 Series, Mercedes S-Class/Maybach, Yangwang U7)."),
    ]
    for m, focus in [
        ("EU", "Climate (winter range, heat), annual mileage and long-distance motorway use, charging infrastructure (public chargers, fast-charging growth), powertrain mix 2025-2026, attitudes to Chinese brands."),
        ("US", "Climate extremes and EV range, annual mileage and commuting, home vs public charging and fast-charging availability, powertrain mix after the tax credit ended, premium buyer attitudes."),
        ("CN", "Climate (north-east winters, south humidity), urban usage and chauffeur/rear-seat culture, charging/battery swap infrastructure, NEV/EREV mix, smart-cockpit culture among premium buyers."),
        ("RoW", "Japan and South Korea premium car markets: usage, compact-car culture, charging infrastructure and powertrain mix (hybrids), import premium brand demand."),
    ]:
        tasks.append(Task(f"mp:{m}", "market_profile_scout", None, None, m, focus))
    # wave-3 'market events' (most recent news, simulated as arriving later)
    tasks += [
        Task("ev:G70:EU:mbos", "competitor_scout", "7 Series", "G70", "EU",
             "Latest 2026 news: Mercedes S-Class facelift / MB.OS features (AI assistant, MB.DRIVE, rear comfort) and customer reception.", wave=3),
        Task("ev:G70:CN:maextro", "competitor_scout", "7 Series", "G70", "CN",
             "Latest 2026 Chinese ultra-luxury launches and updates (Maextro S800, AITO M9/M8, Yangwang U7, Hongqi): new customer-facing features and sales momentum.", wave=3),
        Task("ev:G68:CN:nk", "competitor_scout", "5 Series", "G68", "CN",
             "Latest 2026 news on BMW Neue Klasse iX3 long wheelbase / i3 for China (OS X China, Momenta ADAS, Huawei/Alibaba/DeepSeek features) and how Chinese media and buyers received it versus local rivals.", wave=3),
        Task("ev:G60:US:ev", "market_analyst", "5 Series", "G60", "US",
             "Latest 2026 news on the US EV demand shift (post tax credit), hybrid/PHEV demand and luxury buyers' powertrain preferences.", wave=3),
        Task("ev:G60:EU:eclass", "competitor_scout", "5 Series", "G60", "EU",
             "Latest 2026 news: new Mercedes E-Class / electric C-Class and Audi A6 updates in Europe (MB.OS, AI assistant, charging, range).", wave=3),
        Task("ev:F70:EU:cla", "competitor_scout", "1 Series", "F70", "EU",
             "Latest 2026 news: Mercedes CLA (MB.OS) and Chinese compact premium EVs in Europe - customer-facing features, reviews and early sales.", wave=3),
    ]
    ids = [t.id for t in tasks]
    assert len(ids) == len(set(ids)), "duplicate task ids"
    return tasks


PILOT_TASK_IDS = ["cs:G68:CN", "rm:G60:US", "ts:G60:EU"]

"""Run the web research plan: `uv run python -m bmw_req.research.run [--only-wave N] [--pilot] [--cap-usd X] [--task ID ...]`

Parallel (<= 6 workers), idempotent (a task with a 'web_research' audit_event is skipped), budget-capped.
Stores source_item(kind='web') rows and one audit_event per task (queries, cited URLs, counts).

import hashlib
import json
import logging
import re
import sys
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor, as_completed

import httpx

from bmw_req.db import connect
from bmw_req.llm import LLM, BudgetExceeded
from bmw_req.research.agents import AGENT_VERSION, AGENTS, UA, AgentResult, Task, clean_url, verify_quote
from bmw_req.research.plan import PILOT_TASK_IDS, build_plan

log = logging.getLogger(__name__)
JOB_PREFIX = "research"
MAX_WORKERS = 6


def web_ref(url: str, claim: str) -> str:
    return "web:" + hashlib.sha1((url + claim).encode()).hexdigest()[:12]


def norm_date(s: str | None) -> str | None:
    if not s:
        return None
    m = re.match(r"^(\d{4})(?:-(\d{1,2}))?(?:-(\d{1,2}))?", s.strip())
    if not m:
        return None
    y, mo, d = m.groups()
    return y + (f"-{int(mo):02d}" if mo else "") + (f"-{int(d):02d}" if mo and d else "")


def research_spend(conn) -> float:
    return conn.execute(
        "SELECT COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN status = 'reserved' THEN reserved_usd ELSE cost_usd END), 0) FROM llm_usage "
        "WHERE job LIKE ?", (f"{JOB_PREFIX}:%",)).fetchone()[0]


def done_task_ids(conn) -> set[str]:
    return {r["entity_id"] for r in conn.execute(
        "SELECT entity_id FROM audit_event WHERE action = 'web_research' AND entity_type = 'research_task'")}


def execute(task: Task, verify: bool = True) -> tuple[AgentResult, list[int | None]]:
    """Worker: one agent call (own DB connection) + quote verification. No DB writes besides llm_usage."""
    llm = LLM(conn=connect())
    try:
        res = AGENTS[task.agent](llm, task)
    finally:
        llm.conn.close()
    verified = []
    if verify:
        with httpx.Client(follow_redirects=True, timeout=8.0,
                          headers={"User-Agent": UA, "Accept-Language": "en-US,en;q=0.9"}) as client:
            verified = [verify_quote(clean_url(it.url), it.quote, client=client) for it in res.kept]
    else:
        verified = [None] * len(res.kept)
    return res, verified


def store(conn, res: AgentResult, verified: list[int | None], batch_id: int | None = None) -> list[int]:
    """Persist kept items + the task's audit event in one short transaction. Idempotent on (kind, ref)."""
    t = res.task

            desc = f"web research wave {t.wave} ({AGENT_VERSION})"

                "INSERT INTO ingest_batch (kind, description) VALUES (?, ?)", (kind, desc)).lastrowid
        for it, qv in zip(res.kept, verified):
            url = clean_url(it.url)
            ref = web_ref(url, it.claim)
            meta = {
                "publisher": it.publisher, "evidence_type": it.evidence_type, "competitor": it.competitor,
                "models": it.vehicle_models, "category": it.category, "task_id": t.id, "agent": t.agent,
                "agent_version": AGENT_VERSION, "quote_verified": qv, "query": t.focus, "item_market": it.market_code,
                "llm_usage_id": res.usage_id, "model": res.model,
            }
            conn.execute(
                """INSERT OR IGNORE INTO source_item (kind, ref, external_id, trust_tier, vehicle_model_id, market_code, url,
                   published_at, text, quote, meta_json, ingest_batch_id, wave)
                   VALUES ('web', ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)""",
                (ref, t.id, it.trust_tier, t.vehicle_model_id, t.market_code, url, norm_date(it.published_date),
                 it.claim, it.quote, json.dumps(meta, ensure_ascii=False), batch_id, t.wave))
            ids.append(conn.execute("SELECT id FROM source_item WHERE kind = 'web' AND ref = ?", (ref,)).fetchone()["id"])
        conn.execute(
            """INSERT INTO audit_event (actor_type, actor_id, action, entity_type, entity_id, new_value, rationale, model, prompt_ref)
               VALUES ('ai', ?, 'web_research', 'research_task', ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)""",
            (f"agent:{t.agent}", t.id, json.dumps({
                "queries": res.queries, "cited_urls": sorted(set(res.cited.values())),
                "kept_urls": [clean_url(i.url) for i in res.kept], "dropped_urls": [i.url for i in res.dropped],
                "n_kept": len(res.kept), "n_dropped_uncited": len(res.dropped), "source_item_ids": ids,
                "quote_verified": verified, "wave": t.wave, "vehicle_model_id": t.vehicle_model_id,
                "market_code": t.market_code, "llm_usage_id": res.usage_id, "cost_usd": res.cost_usd,
            }, ensure_ascii=False), f"Web research task: {t.focus}", res.model, AGENT_VERSION))
        conn.execute("COMMIT")
    except BaseException:
        conn.execute("ROLLBACK")
        raise
    return ids


def main(argv=None) -> None:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--only-wave", type=int)
    ap.add_argument("--pilot", action="store_true")
    ap.add_argument("--cap-usd", type=float, default=4.5, help="stop submitting when research spend reaches this")
    ap.add_argument("--task", nargs="*", help="run only these task ids")
    ap.add_argument("--workers", type=int, default=MAX_WORKERS)
    args = ap.parse_args(argv)
    logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO, format="%(asctime)s %(message)s")

    conn = connect()
    tasks = build_plan()
    if args.pilot:
        tasks = [t for t in tasks if t.id in PILOT_TASK_IDS]
    if args.task:
        tasks = [t for t in tasks if t.id in set(args.task)]
    if args.only_wave is not None:
        tasks = [t for t in tasks if t.wave == args.only_wave]
    done = done_task_ids(conn)
    todo = [t for t in tasks if t.id not in done]
    log.info("plan: %d tasks selected, %d already done, %d to run; research spend so far $%.4f",
             len(tasks), len(tasks) - len(todo), len(todo), research_spend(conn))

    # Worst case per task ~ $0.04 search + ~$0.02 tokens; keep a margin under the cap.
    per_task_margin = 0.08
    totals = {"kept": 0, "dropped": 0, "verified": 0, "unverified": 0, "unfetchable": 0, "failed": 0}
    with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=min(args.workers, MAX_WORKERS)) as pool:
        futures, queue = {}, list(todo)
        while queue or futures:
            while queue and len(futures) < args.workers:
                if research_spend(conn) + per_task_margin * (len(futures) + 1) > args.cap_usd:
                    log.warning("cap $%.2f reached; %d tasks not started", args.cap_usd, len(queue))
                    queue = []
                    break
                t = queue.pop(0)
                futures[pool.submit(execute, t)] = t
            if not futures:
                break
            fut = next(as_completed(futures))
            t = futures.pop(fut)
            try:
                res, verified = fut.result()
            except BudgetExceeded as e:
                log.error("budget guard: %s", e)
                queue = []
                totals["failed"] += 1
                continue
            except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001 - keep the batch going, task stays not-done
                log.error("task %s failed: %r", t.id, e)
                totals["failed"] += 1
                continue
            ids = store(conn, res, verified)
            totals["kept"] += len(res.kept)
            totals["dropped"] += len(res.dropped)
            totals["verified"] += sum(1 for v in verified if v == 1)
            totals["unverified"] += sum(1 for v in verified if v == 0)
            totals["unfetchable"] += sum(1 for v in verified if v is None)
            log.info("%-22s kept %d dropped %d verified %s ids %s $%.4f", t.id, len(res.kept), len(res.dropped),
                     verified, ids, res.cost_usd)
    log.info("done: %s; research spend $%.4f", totals, research_spend(conn))
    if totals["failed"]:
        sys.exit(1)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""Run the web research plan: `uv run python -m bmw_req.research.run [--only-wave N] [--pilot] [--cap-usd X] [--task ID ...]`

Parallel (<= 6 workers), idempotent (a task with a 'web_research' audit_event is skipped), budget-capped.
Stores source_item(kind='web') rows and one audit_event per task (queries, cited URLs, counts).
"""

import argparse
import hashlib
import json
import logging
import re
import sys
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor, as_completed

import httpx

from bmw_req.db import connect
from bmw_req.llm import LLM, BudgetExceeded
from bmw_req.research.agents import AGENT_VERSION, AGENTS, UA, AgentResult, Task, clean_url, verify_quote
from bmw_req.research.plan import PILOT_TASK_IDS, build_plan

log = logging.getLogger(__name__)
JOB_PREFIX = "research"
MAX_WORKERS = 6


def web_ref(url: str, claim: str) -> str:
    return "web:" + hashlib.sha1((url + claim).encode()).hexdigest()[:12]


def norm_date(s: str | None) -> str | None:
    if not s:
        return None
    m = re.match(r"^(\d{4})(?:-(\d{1,2}))?(?:-(\d{1,2}))?", s.strip())
    if not m:
        return None
    y, mo, d = m.groups()
    return y + (f"-{int(mo):02d}" if mo else "") + (f"-{int(d):02d}" if mo and d else "")


def research_spend(conn) -> float:
    return conn.execute(
        "SELECT COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN status = 'reserved' THEN reserved_usd ELSE cost_usd END), 0) FROM llm_usage "
        "WHERE job LIKE ?", (f"{JOB_PREFIX}:%",)).fetchone()[0]


def done_task_ids(conn) -> set[str]:
    return {r["entity_id"] for r in conn.execute(
        "SELECT entity_id FROM audit_event WHERE action = 'web_research' AND entity_type = 'research_task'")}


def execute(task: Task, verify: bool = True) -> tuple[AgentResult, list[int | None]]:
    """Worker: one agent call (own DB connection) + quote verification. No DB writes besides llm_usage."""
    llm = LLM(conn=connect())
    try:
        res = AGENTS[task.agent](llm, task)
    finally:
        llm.conn.close()
    verified = []
    if verify:
        with httpx.Client(follow_redirects=True, timeout=8.0,
                          headers={"User-Agent": UA, "Accept-Language": "en-US,en;q=0.9"}) as client:
            verified = [verify_quote(clean_url(it.url), it.quote, client=client) for it in res.kept]
    else:
        verified = [None] * len(res.kept)
    return res, verified


def store(conn, res: AgentResult, verified: list[int | None], batch_id: int | None = None) -> list[int]:
    """Persist kept items + the task's audit event in one short transaction. Idempotent on (kind, ref)."""
    t = res.task
    ids = []
    conn.execute("BEGIN IMMEDIATE")
    try:
        if batch_id is None:
            kind = "competitor_event" if t.wave > 1 else "web_refresh"
            desc = f"web research wave {t.wave} ({AGENT_VERSION})"
            row = conn.execute("SELECT id FROM ingest_batch WHERE kind = ? AND description = ?", (kind, desc)).fetchone()
            batch_id = row["id"] if row else conn.execute(
                "INSERT INTO ingest_batch (kind, description) VALUES (?, ?)", (kind, desc)).lastrowid
        for it, qv in zip(res.kept, verified):
            url = clean_url(it.url)
            ref = web_ref(url, it.claim)
            meta = {
                "publisher": it.publisher, "evidence_type": it.evidence_type, "competitor": it.competitor,
                "models": it.vehicle_models, "category": it.category, "task_id": t.id, "agent": t.agent,
                "agent_version": AGENT_VERSION, "quote_verified": qv, "query": t.focus, "item_market": it.market_code,
                "llm_usage_id": res.usage_id, "model": res.model,
            }
            conn.execute(
                """INSERT OR IGNORE INTO source_item (kind, ref, external_id, trust_tier, vehicle_model_id, market_code, url,
                   published_at, text, quote, meta_json, ingest_batch_id, wave)
                   VALUES ('web', ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)""",
                (ref, t.id, it.trust_tier, t.vehicle_model_id, t.market_code, url, norm_date(it.published_date),
                 it.claim, it.quote, json.dumps(meta, ensure_ascii=False), batch_id, t.wave))
            ids.append(conn.execute("SELECT id FROM source_item WHERE kind = 'web' AND ref = ?", (ref,)).fetchone()["id"])
        conn.execute(
            """INSERT INTO audit_event (actor_type, actor_id, action, entity_type, entity_id, new_value, rationale, model, prompt_ref)
               VALUES ('ai', ?, 'web_research', 'research_task', ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)""",
            (f"agent:{t.agent}", t.id, json.dumps({
                "queries": res.queries, "cited_urls": sorted(set(res.cited.values())),
                "kept_urls": [clean_url(i.url) for i in res.kept], "dropped_urls": [i.url for i in res.dropped],
                "n_kept": len(res.kept), "n_dropped_uncited": len(res.dropped), "source_item_ids": ids,
                "quote_verified": verified, "wave": t.wave, "vehicle_model_id": t.vehicle_model_id,
                "market_code": t.market_code, "llm_usage_id": res.usage_id, "cost_usd": res.cost_usd,
            }, ensure_ascii=False), f"Web research task: {t.focus}", res.model, AGENT_VERSION))
        conn.execute("COMMIT")
    except BaseException:
        conn.execute("ROLLBACK")
        raise
    return ids


def main(argv=None) -> None:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--only-wave", type=int)
    ap.add_argument("--pilot", action="store_true")
    ap.add_argument("--cap-usd", type=float, default=4.5, help="stop submitting when research spend reaches this")
    ap.add_argument("--task", nargs="*", help="run only these task ids")
    ap.add_argument("--workers", type=int, default=MAX_WORKERS)
    args = ap.parse_args(argv)
    logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO, format="%(asctime)s %(message)s")

    conn = connect()
    tasks = build_plan()
    if args.pilot:
        tasks = [t for t in tasks if t.id in PILOT_TASK_IDS]
    if args.task:
        tasks = [t for t in tasks if t.id in set(args.task)]
    if args.only_wave is not None:
        tasks = [t for t in tasks if t.wave == args.only_wave]
    done = done_task_ids(conn)
    todo = [t for t in tasks if t.id not in done]
    log.info("plan: %d tasks selected, %d already done, %d to run; research spend so far $%.4f",
             len(tasks), len(tasks) - len(todo), len(todo), research_spend(conn))

    # Worst case per task ~ $0.04 search + ~$0.02 tokens; keep a margin under the cap.
    per_task_margin = 0.08
    totals = {"kept": 0, "dropped": 0, "verified": 0, "unverified": 0, "unfetchable": 0, "failed": 0}
    with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=min(args.workers, MAX_WORKERS)) as pool:
        futures, queue = {}, list(todo)
        while queue or futures:
            while queue and len(futures) < args.workers:
                if research_spend(conn) + per_task_margin * (len(futures) + 1) > args.cap_usd:
                    log.warning("cap $%.2f reached; %d tasks not started", args.cap_usd, len(queue))
                    queue = []
                    break
                t = queue.pop(0)
                futures[pool.submit(execute, t)] = t
            if not futures:
                break
            fut = next(as_completed(futures))
            t = futures.pop(fut)
            try:
                res, verified = fut.result()
            except BudgetExceeded as e:
                log.error("budget guard: %s", e)
                queue = []
                totals["failed"] += 1
                continue
            except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001 - keep the batch going, task stays not-done
                log.error("task %s failed: %r", t.id, e)
                totals["failed"] += 1
                continue
            ids = store(conn, res, verified)
            totals["kept"] += len(res.kept)
            totals["dropped"] += len(res.dropped)
            totals["verified"] += sum(1 for v in verified if v == 1)
            totals["unverified"] += sum(1 for v in verified if v == 0)
            totals["unfetchable"] += sum(1 for v in verified if v is None)
            log.info("%-22s kept %d dropped %d verified %s ids %s $%.4f", t.id, len(res.kept), len(res.dropped),
                     verified, ids, res.cost_usd)
    log.info("done: %s; research spend $%.4f", totals, research_spend(conn))
    if totals["failed"]:
        sys.exit(1)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""Web findings: group web evidence per (derivative, market, wave) and let luna cluster it into findings.

`uv run python -m bmw_req.research.findings [--only-wave N]` — one LLM call per group, idempotent per group
(audit_event action 'build_web_findings'). Every finding links >= 1 source item of its group (IDs validated);
conflicting items are linked with relation 'contradicts'. Wave-1 and wave-3 items are grouped separately so that
'market event' evidence surfaces as findings with first_wave = 3.
"""

import argparse
import json
import logging
from collections import defaultdict
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
from typing import Literal

from pydantic import BaseModel, Field

from bmw_req.db import connect
from bmw_req.llm import LLM
from bmw_req.pipeline.extract import Category

log = logging.getLogger(__name__)
FINDINGS_VERSION = "web-findings-v1"
JOB = "research:findings"

FindingType = Literal["competitor_advantage", "market_trend", "customer_expectation", "review_criticism",
                      "review_praise", "market_profile"]


class WebFinding(BaseModel):
    type: FindingType
    title: str = Field(description="Short, factual title (max ~12 words)")
    summary: str = Field(description="2-4 factual sentences that only restate the cited items; mention conflicts")
    category: Category | None
    scope_level: Literal["market", "derivative"] = Field(
        description="'derivative' if about this BMW model or its direct rivals, 'market' if a market-wide trend/profile")
    supporting_ids: list[int] = Field(description="IDs of the items that support this finding (>= 1)")
    contradicting_ids: list[int] = Field(description="IDs of items that contradict or qualify it (may be empty)")


class FindingsOut(BaseModel):
    findings: list[WebFinding]


INSTRUCTIONS = """You group cited web evidence items into findings for a BMW product-requirements team.
- Merge items that state the same point; one item may support several findings. Use only the given item IDs.
- Finding types: competitor_advantage (a rival offers customers something BMW lacks/does worse), market_trend,
  customer_expectation (what buyers expect now or in 3-5 years), review_criticism / review_praise (professional
  reviews; say which model), market_profile (climate, usage, culture, infrastructure, powertrain mix).
- Summaries are factual and cite nothing beyond the items; no recommendations, no opinions.
- If items disagree (e.g. different figures or verdicts), keep both: put the disagreeing ones in contradicting_ids
  and say so in the summary. Do not hide conflicting evidence.
- Every item should end up in at least one finding."""


def load_groups(conn, only_wave: int | None = None) -> dict[tuple, list[dict]]:
    groups = defaultdict(list)
    for r in conn.execute("SELECT id, trust_tier, vehicle_model_id, market_code, url, published_at, text, quote, meta_json, wave "
                          "FROM source_item WHERE kind = 'web' ORDER BY id"):
        if only_wave is not None and r["wave"] != only_wave:
            continue
        m = json.loads(r["meta_json"] or "{}")
        groups[(r["vehicle_model_id"], r["market_code"], r["wave"])].append({
            "id": r["id"], "tier": r["trust_tier"], "publisher": m.get("publisher"), "date": r["published_at"],
            "evidence_type": m.get("evidence_type"), "category": m.get("category"), "competitor": m.get("competitor"),
            "claim": r["text"], "quote": (r["quote"] or "")[:300], "url": r["url"], "wave": r["wave"],
        })
    return dict(groups)


def group_key(g: tuple) -> str:
    vm, mk, wave = g
    return f"{vm or '-'}|{mk}|w{wave}"


def validate(out: FindingsOut, items: list[dict]) -> tuple[list[WebFinding], dict]:
    """Keep only IDs from the group; drop findings without valid support. Returns (findings, stats)."""
    valid = {i["id"] for i in items}
    kept, stats = [], {"dropped_findings": 0, "invalid_ids": 0, "uncovered_items": 0}
    for f in out.findings:
        sup = [i for i in dict.fromkeys(f.supporting_ids) if i in valid]
        con = [i for i in dict.fromkeys(f.contradicting_ids) if i in valid and i not in sup]
        stats["invalid_ids"] += (len(set(f.supporting_ids) | set(f.contradicting_ids)) - len(set(sup) | set(con)))
        if not sup:
            stats["dropped_findings"] += 1
            continue
        kept.append(f.model_copy(update={"supporting_ids": sup, "contradicting_ids": con}))
    covered = {i for f in kept for i in f.supporting_ids + f.contradicting_ids}
    stats["uncovered_items"] = len(valid - covered)
    return kept, stats


def metrics(ids: list[int], by_id: dict[int, dict]) -> dict:
    its = [by_id[i] for i in ids]
    tiers = defaultdict(int)
    for i in its:
        tiers[i["tier"]] += 1
    dates = [i["date"] for i in its if i["date"]]
    return {"n_sources": len(its), "tiers": dict(tiers), "publishers": sorted({i["publisher"] for i in its if i["publisher"]}),
            "newest_date": max(dates) if dates else None}


def build_group(llm: LLM, g: tuple, items: list[dict]):
    vm, mk, wave = g
    header = f"Derivative: {vm or 'none (market-level)'}; market: {mk}; wave: {wave}; {len(items)} items."
    payload = [{k: i[k] for k in ("id", "tier", "publisher", "date", "evidence_type", "category", "competitor", "claim", "quote")}
               for i in items]
    res = llm.generate(job=JOB, tier="fast", instructions=INSTRUCTIONS,
                       input=header + "\nItems:\n" + json.dumps(payload, ensure_ascii=False),
                       schema=FindingsOut, reasoning_effort="low", max_output_tokens=8000)
    return res


def store_group(conn, g: tuple, items: list[dict], findings: list[WebFinding], stats: dict, model: str, usage_id) -> list[int]:
    vm, mk, wave = g
    by_id = {i["id"]: i for i in items}
    ids = []
    conn.execute("BEGIN IMMEDIATE")
    try:
        for f in findings:
            linked = f.supporting_ids + f.contradicting_ids
            scope = "market" if vm is None else f.scope_level
            m = metrics(linked, by_id)
            m["n_supporting"], m["n_contradicting"] = len(f.supporting_ids), len(f.contradicting_ids)
            m["builder"] = FINDINGS_VERSION
            fid = conn.execute(
                """INSERT INTO finding (type, title, summary, scope_level, vehicle_model_id, market_code, metrics_json, created_by,
                   source_kind, polarity, category, first_wave) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, 'web', 'context', ?, ?)""",
                (f.type, f.title, f.summary, scope, vm if scope == "derivative" else None, mk, json.dumps(m, ensure_ascii=False),
                 f"ai:{model}", f.category, min(by_id[i]["wave"] for i in linked))).lastrowid
            for i in f.supporting_ids:
                conn.execute("INSERT INTO finding_source (finding_id, source_item_id, quote, relation) VALUES (?, ?, ?, 'supports')",
                             (fid, i, by_id[i]["quote"]))
            for i in f.contradicting_ids:
                conn.execute("INSERT INTO finding_source (finding_id, source_item_id, quote, relation) VALUES (?, ?, ?, 'contradicts')",
                             (fid, i, by_id[i]["quote"]))
            ids.append(fid)
        conn.execute(
            """INSERT INTO audit_event (actor_type, actor_id, action, entity_type, entity_id, new_value, rationale, model, prompt_ref)
               VALUES ('ai', 'research.findings', 'build_web_findings', 'finding_group', ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)""",
            (group_key(g), json.dumps({"finding_ids": ids, "n_items": len(items), "llm_usage_id": usage_id, **stats}),
             "Clustered cited web evidence into findings (status: proposed context for derivation).", model, FINDINGS_VERSION))
        conn.execute("COMMIT")
    except BaseException:
        conn.execute("ROLLBACK")
        raise
    return ids


def done_groups(conn) -> set[str]:
    return {r["entity_id"] for r in conn.execute("SELECT entity_id FROM audit_event WHERE action = 'build_web_findings'")}


def build_all(conn, llm_factory=None, only_wave: int | None = None, workers: int = 4) -> dict:
    llm_factory = llm_factory or (lambda: LLM(conn=connect()))
    groups = load_groups(conn, only_wave)
    done = done_groups(conn)
    todo = {g: its for g, its in groups.items() if group_key(g) not in done}
    summary = {}

    def work(g):
        llm = llm_factory()
        return g, build_group(llm, g, todo[g]), llm.model_for("fast")

    with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=workers) as pool:
        for g, res, model in pool.map(work, list(todo)):
            findings, stats = validate(res.parsed, todo[g])
            ids = store_group(conn, g, todo[g], findings, stats, model, res.usage_id)
            summary[group_key(g)] = {"items": len(todo[g]), "findings": len(ids), **stats, "cost_usd": res.cost_usd}
            log.info("%s: %s", group_key(g), summary[group_key(g)])
    return summary


def main(argv=None):
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--only-wave", type=int)
    args = ap.parse_args(argv)
    logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO, format="%(asctime)s %(message)s")
    print(json.dumps(build_all(connect(), only_wave=args.only_wave), indent=1))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""Web findings: group web evidence per (derivative, market, wave) and let luna cluster it into findings.

`uv run python -m bmw_req.research.findings [--only-wave N]` — one LLM call per group, idempotent per group
(audit_event action 'build_web_findings'). Every finding links >= 1 source item of its group (IDs validated);
conflicting items are linked with relation 'contradicts'. Wave-1 and wave-3 items are grouped separately so that
'market event' evidence surfaces as findings with first_wave = 3.
"""

import argparse
import json
import logging
from collections import defaultdict
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
from typing import Literal

from pydantic import BaseModel, Field

from bmw_req.db import connect
from bmw_req.llm import LLM
from bmw_req.pipeline.extract import Category

log = logging.getLogger(__name__)
FINDINGS_VERSION = "web-findings-v1"
JOB = "research:findings"

FindingType = Literal["competitor_advantage", "market_trend", "customer_expectation", "review_criticism",
                      "review_praise", "market_profile"]


class WebFinding(BaseModel):
    type: FindingType
    title: str = Field(description="Short, factual title (max ~12 words)")
    summary: str = Field(description="2-4 factual sentences that only restate the cited items; mention conflicts")
    category: Category | None
    scope_level: Literal["market", "derivative"] = Field(
        description="'derivative' if about this BMW model or its direct rivals, 'market' if a market-wide trend/profile")
    supporting_ids: list[int] = Field(description="IDs of the items that support this finding (>= 1)")
    contradicting_ids: list[int] = Field(description="IDs of items that contradict or qualify it (may be empty)")


class FindingsOut(BaseModel):
    findings: list[WebFinding]


INSTRUCTIONS = """You group cited web evidence items into findings for a BMW product-requirements team.
- Merge items that state the same point; one item may support several findings. Use only the given item IDs.
- Finding types: competitor_advantage (a rival offers customers something BMW lacks/does worse), market_trend,
  customer_expectation (what buyers expect now or in 3-5 years), review_criticism / review_praise (professional
  reviews; say which model), market_profile (climate, usage, culture, infrastructure, powertrain mix).
- Summaries are factual and cite nothing beyond the items; no recommendations, no opinions.
- If items disagree (e.g. different figures or verdicts), keep both: put the disagreeing ones in contradicting_ids
  and say so in the summary. Do not hide conflicting evidence.
- Every item should end up in at least one finding."""


def load_groups(conn, only_wave: int | None = None) -> dict[tuple, list[dict]]:
    groups = defaultdict(list)
    for r in conn.execute("SELECT id, trust_tier, vehicle_model_id, market_code, url, published_at, text, quote, meta_json, wave "
                          "FROM source_item WHERE kind = 'web' ORDER BY id"):
        if only_wave is not None and r["wave"] != only_wave:
            continue
        m = json.loads(r["meta_json"] or "{}")
        groups[(r["vehicle_model_id"], r["market_code"], r["wave"])].append({
            "id": r["id"], "tier": r["trust_tier"], "publisher": m.get("publisher"), "date": r["published_at"],
            "evidence_type": m.get("evidence_type"), "category": m.get("category"), "competitor": m.get("competitor"),
            "claim": r["text"], "quote": (r["quote"] or "")[:300], "url": r["url"], "wave": r["wave"],
        })
    return dict(groups)


def group_key(g: tuple) -> str:
    vm, mk, wave = g
    return f"{vm or '-'}|{mk}|w{wave}"


def validate(out: FindingsOut, items: list[dict]) -> tuple[list[WebFinding], dict]:
    """Keep only IDs from the group; drop findings without valid support. Returns (findings, stats)."""
    valid = {i["id"] for i in items}
    kept, stats = [], {"dropped_findings": 0, "invalid_ids": 0, "uncovered_items": 0}
    for f in out.findings:
        sup = [i for i in dict.fromkeys(f.supporting_ids) if i in valid]
        con = [i for i in dict.fromkeys(f.contradicting_ids) if i in valid and i not in sup]
        stats["invalid_ids"] += (len(set(f.supporting_ids) | set(f.contradicting_ids)) - len(set(sup) | set(con)))
        if not sup:
            stats["dropped_findings"] += 1
            continue
        kept.append(f.model_copy(update={"supporting_ids": sup, "contradicting_ids": con}))
    covered = {i for f in kept for i in f.supporting_ids + f.contradicting_ids}
    stats["uncovered_items"] = len(valid - covered)
    return kept, stats


def metrics(ids: list[int], by_id: dict[int, dict]) -> dict:
    its = [by_id[i] for i in ids]
    tiers = defaultdict(int)
    for i in its:
        tiers[i["tier"]] += 1
    dates = [i["date"] for i in its if i["date"]]
    return {"n_sources": len(its), "tiers": dict(tiers), "publishers": sorted({i["publisher"] for i in its if i["publisher"]}),
            "newest_date": max(dates) if dates else None}


def build_group(llm: LLM, g: tuple, items: list[dict]):
    vm, mk, wave = g
    header = f"Derivative: {vm or 'none (market-level)'}; market: {mk}; wave: {wave}; {len(items)} items."
    payload = [{k: i[k] for k in ("id", "tier", "publisher", "date", "evidence_type", "category", "competitor", "claim", "quote")}
               for i in items]
    res = llm.generate(job=JOB, tier="fast", instructions=INSTRUCTIONS,
                       input=header + "\nItems:\n" + json.dumps(payload, ensure_ascii=False),
                       schema=FindingsOut, reasoning_effort="low", max_output_tokens=8000)
    return res


def store_group(conn, g: tuple, items: list[dict], findings: list[WebFinding], stats: dict, model: str, usage_id) -> list[int]:
    vm, mk, wave = g
    by_id = {i["id"]: i for i in items}
    ids = []
    conn.execute("BEGIN IMMEDIATE")
    try:
        for f in findings:
            linked = f.supporting_ids + f.contradicting_ids
            scope = "market" if vm is None else f.scope_level
            m = metrics(linked, by_id)
            m["n_supporting"], m["n_contradicting"] = len(f.supporting_ids), len(f.contradicting_ids)
            m["builder"] = FINDINGS_VERSION
            fid = conn.execute(
                """INSERT INTO finding (type, title, summary, scope_level, vehicle_model_id, market_code, metrics_json, created_by,
                   source_kind, polarity, category, first_wave) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, 'web', 'context', ?, ?)""",
                (f.type, f.title, f.summary, scope, vm if scope == "derivative" else None, mk, json.dumps(m, ensure_ascii=False),
                 f"ai:{model}", f.category, min(by_id[i]["wave"] for i in linked))).lastrowid
            for i in f.supporting_ids:
                conn.execute("INSERT INTO finding_source (finding_id, source_item_id, quote, relation) VALUES (?, ?, ?, 'supports')",
                             (fid, i, by_id[i]["quote"]))
            for i in f.contradicting_ids:
                conn.execute("INSERT INTO finding_source (finding_id, source_item_id, quote, relation) VALUES (?, ?, ?, 'contradicts')",
                             (fid, i, by_id[i]["quote"]))
            ids.append(fid)
        conn.execute(
            """INSERT INTO audit_event (actor_type, actor_id, action, entity_type, entity_id, new_value, rationale, model, prompt_ref)
               VALUES ('ai', 'research.findings', 'build_web_findings', 'finding_group', ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)""",
            (group_key(g), json.dumps({"finding_ids": ids, "n_items": len(items), "llm_usage_id": usage_id, **stats}),
             "Clustered cited web evidence into findings (status: proposed context for derivation).", model, FINDINGS_VERSION))
        conn.execute("COMMIT")
    except BaseException:
        conn.execute("ROLLBACK")
        raise
    return ids


def done_groups(conn) -> set[str]:
    return {r["entity_id"] for r in conn.execute("SELECT entity_id FROM audit_event WHERE action = 'build_web_findings'")}


def build_all(conn, llm_factory=None, only_wave: int | None = None, workers: int = 4) -> dict:
    llm_factory = llm_factory or (lambda: LLM(conn=connect()))
    groups = load_groups(conn, only_wave)
    done = done_groups(conn)
    todo = {g: its for g, its in groups.items() if group_key(g) not in done}
    summary = {}

    def work(g):
        llm = llm_factory()
        return g, build_group(llm, g, todo[g]), llm.model_for("fast")

    with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=workers) as pool:
        for g, res, model in pool.map(work, list(todo)):
            findings, stats = validate(res.parsed, todo[g])
            ids = store_group(conn, g, todo[g], findings, stats, model, res.usage_id)
            summary[group_key(g)] = {"items": len(todo[g]), "findings": len(ids), **stats, "cost_usd": res.cost_usd}
            log.info("%s: %s", group_key(g), summary[group_key(g)])
    return summary


def main(argv=None):
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--only-wave", type=int)
    args = ap.parse_args(argv)
    logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO, format="%(asctime)s %(message)s")
    print(json.dumps(build_all(connect(), only_wave=args.only_wave), indent=1))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
